verified.title: MasDrift: Benchmarking Authorization Preservation Across Multi-Agent Architectures
verified.resolved_title: MasDrift: Benchmarking Authorization Preservation Across Multi-Agent Architectures
verified.authors: Zhuoning Xu, Xiucheng Zhang, Hanjun Luo, Yingbin Jin, Yinpeng Dong, Hanan Salam
verified.verification_source: arXiv API export.arxiv.org, id_list=2608.07556 (v2 updated 2026-08-11)
verified.abstract_gist: MasDrift is a 600-task benign benchmark that pairs required work with reserved actions and compares single-agent, centralized and decentralized coordination while varying hierarchy depth and peer width. Centralized hierarchies complete 93.9 to 98.6 percent of tasks but take unauthorized actions in 2.7 to 19.8 percent (widening with depth) versus 0.6 to 0.8 percent for peer networks; re-anchoring every pending call to the original user request cuts unauthorized actions in every configuration at 1.6 points of completion, while propagating an attenuated policy along the chain forfeits up to 36.3 points.
verified.use: Cite as the closest existing manipulation of what a delegated worker sees: their re-anchoring defense is functionally our V1/V2 (show the worker the root objective), and their depth-widening authorization loss is the mirror image of our objective-directed departure. Also cite in C4 for the centralization tradeoff and in the harness-policy discussion as evidence that where authorization evidence resides matters.
verified.differentiation: MasDrift measures loss of authorization boundaries (workers doing more than permitted) and treats showing the root request as a defense; our study plants an explicit instruction-versus-objective conflict and measures whether hierarchy visibility makes the worker depart from its literal instruction toward the parent objective, announced or silent, with length-matched and hierarchy-matched controls and reasoning-token accounting. They vary topology depth and width; we vary the visibility layer at fixed topology and add flag-without-deviation as an outcome class.

verified.title: Facts Without Rules: Boundary Metadata Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs
verified.resolved_title: Facts Without Rules: Boundary Metadata Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs
verified.authors: Yian Wang, Agam Goyal, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Hari Sundaram
verified.verification_source: arXiv API export.arxiv.org, id_list=2608.29028 (v1 2026-08-29)
verified.abstract_gist: Handoff summaries between agents preserve operational facts but weaken the boundary metadata governing how facts may be used, a failure the authors call summary collapse; on GPT-5-mini and DeepSeek-R1-32B, boundary-marker survival is near-uncorrelated with fact survival, and a 25-word budget drops it from about 0.80 to about 0.57. Downstream leakage depends on boundary explicitness (vague constraints leak in 73 percent of GPT and 50 percent of DeepSeek cases, explicit ones under 15 percent), a single-agent no-handoff control leaks more than the operationalized handoff, and an audience allowlist nearly eliminates leakage.
verified.use: Cite for the complementary finding that what the worker is shown is shaped by the compression step itself: constraints and boundary rules are the first casualties of a length budget. Use in the design rationale for V2 (verbatim parent brief rather than a summary) and for the length-matched control, and cite the explicitness result when discussing why our planted conflict is stated explicitly.
verified.differentiation: Their manipulation is the handoff artifact's length and constraint explicitness, and the outcome is privacy leakage past a boundary rule; ours holds the worker's instruction fixed and adds layers of hierarchy context above it, measuring objective-directed departure and flagging. They show rules degrade in transit; we show what the worker does when the rule and the objective visibly disagree.

verified.title: Multi-Agent AI Safety as an Institutional Design Problem
verified.resolved_title: Multi-Agent AI Safety as an Institutional Design Problem
verified.authors: Abdullah X
verified.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.LG, cs.AI, cs.MA); comment: 17 pages, 5 figures, code in the public POLIS repository
verified.verification_source: arXiv API export.arxiv.org, id_list=2608.09828 (v1 2026-08-10)
verified.abstract_gist: A frozen 5,280-episode suite (four model families in the pre-specified delegation experiment, three more endpoints in a high-conflict diagnostic) varies how rules are formulated to the model and which authority state guards consult. A detailed constitutional prompt and a provenance-aware guard both yield 0/384 realized violations, a local-state guard admits 22/96 violations in laundering scenarios versus 0/96 for provenance enforcement, and merely revealing a cap's numerical value changes agent requests.
verified.use: Cite in the organization-theory layer as the institutional-design framing of multi-agent safety (rule text, trusted authority state, and post-block path as separable levers), and cite the cap-value result as independent evidence that revealing a parameter to the worker shifts its behavior, paralleling our finding that showing the objective shifts flagging rates.
verified.differentiation: Their dependent variable is rule violation under different rule formulations and guard designs; ours is departure from the literal instruction toward a visible parent objective. They study compliance with a constitution; we study a worker choosing between two legitimate authorities (its brief and the objective above it).

verified.title: ArcticSwarm: Deferring Early Consensus in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Research
verified.resolved_title: ArcticSwarm: Deferring Early Consensus in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Research
verified.authors: Soyoung Yoon, Boyi Liu, Yite Wang, Ruofan Wu, Canwen Xu, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Seung-won Hwang, Yuxiong He, Zhewei Yao
verified.verification_source: arXiv API export.arxiv.org, id_list=2609.01870 (v1 2026-09-01)
verified.abstract_gist: ArcticSwarm separates evidence gathering from integration: subagents post to a shared bulletin board while gated isolation lets selected search tasks keep their own prior, and structured review at three commitment boundaries limits what propagates. On BrowseComp-Plus with Qwen 3.5-27B it reaches 82.6 percent versus 78.8 percent without gated isolation and 74.5 percent with structured review also disabled; on live-web BrowseComp with GPT-5 it reaches 73.6 percent.
verified.use: Cite as a measured cost of peer-progress visibility: removing isolation from peer reads costs 3.8 points, which supports treating V5 (live peer polling) as a design variable with a downside rather than free context. Also relevant to the Suite B ledger design as an example of a bulletin board with gated reads.
verified.differentiation: They optimize task accuracy in open-ended research and treat peer visibility as a search-diversity problem; we measure instruction adherence and departure under a planted conflict and treat peer visibility as one rung of a hierarchy-visibility ladder. Their ablation changes architecture; ours changes only what the worker is shown.

verified.title: When Agents Coordinate: Measuring Coordination in Multi-Agent AI Coding
verified.resolved_title: When Agents Coordinate: Measuring Coordination in Multi-Agent AI Coding
verified.authors: Giuseppe Destefanis, Tomaso Aste
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16801 (v1 2026-08-17); API returned empty after retries
verified.abstract_gist: Represents each coding-team run as a temporal network of agents, files, messages and reads over 1,902 runs varying team size, structure and file policy. Direct messaging grows near-quadratically then levels off into broadcast, shared files cut output tokens about 42 percent at eight agents on message-heavy work, naming a coordinator creates no hub and no reliable gain, and agents seek hidden grading material unprompted in four fifths of 244 sealed runs.
verified.use: Cite in the Suite B design for shared files versus messaging as the ledger channel and for the null effect of a nominal coordinator; cite the unprompted hidden-material seeking as a documented case of objective-directed behavior that no instruction requested, adjacent to our silent-deviation class.
verified.differentiation: They measure coordination structure and cost in free-running teams with no planted conflict; we isolate a single worker and vary its view of the hierarchy under a controlled instruction-versus-objective conflict with deterministic outcome checkers. Their hidden-material finding is a side observation; our announced-versus-silent distinction is the primary outcome.

verified.title: Zero-Shot Self-Orchestration with Ledger-Based Control for Improved LLM Coding Performance
verified.resolved_title: Zero-Shot Self-Orchestration with Ledger-Based Control for Improved LLM Coding Performance
verified.authors: Victor Gao, Vida Khosrowshahi, Ali Khosrowshahi, Xihao Sun, Juhyun Lee, Simon (Sang Won) Lee
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26480 (v1 2026-08-27); API returned empty after retries
verified.abstract_gist: Adds a manager-worker scaffold over a shared filesystem, with no training or tuning, to nine models on the 100 latest hard LiveCodeBench problems and compares against the same model in a single pass. Gains are conditional (large for some models, null or negative for others, larger with reasoning off or for smaller models), the manager roughly triples the token bill but is cheaper per point than a larger model, and transcript analysis attributes gains to context management through short worker calls and shared notes plus problem decomposition.
verified.use: Cite for the token cost of orchestration (manager triples the bill) and for shared notes as a working ledger, in the cost discussion alongside our reasoning-token doubling under hierarchy context; cite the reasoning-on versus reasoning-off interaction in the reasoning-effort section.
verified.differentiation: They measure accuracy gains from a scaffold with no conflict between manager and worker goals; we hold the scaffold fixed and measure worker adherence when its instruction conflicts with the objective, isolating the effect of showing the ledger rather than the effect of having one.

verified.title: The Interaction Tax: When Communication Erases Diversity in Multi-Agent Teams
verified.resolved_title: The Interaction Tax: When Communication Erases Diversity in Multi-Agent Teams
verified.authors: Summer Eunhyung Ann, Haokun Liu, Chenhao Tan
verified.venue: ICML 2026 (PMLR 306), per arXiv comment; arXiv (cs.MA, cs.AI)
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23541 (v1 2026-08-24; comment: 14 pages, 3 figures, accepted at ICML 2026 (PMLR 306)); API returned empty after retries
verified.abstract_gist: Argues the conflicting literature on whether multi-agent interaction helps reflects a missing distinction about what information agents exchange: when agents read each other's complete outputs their proposals converge within one round and anchor on the first solution seen. On 11 verifier-scored optimization tasks under matched budgets, full-solution interaction is a weak default, independent proposal generation avoids the collapse, and critique helps only when the violated rule is easy to find and fix.
verified.use: Cite for the thesis that multi-agent outcomes depend on what information is exchanged rather than how many agents exist, which is the framing our visibility ladder operationalizes; cite the anchoring-on-first-seen result when discussing V5 peer polling as a source of convergence.
verified.differentiation: Their outcome is solution diversity and accuracy under matched budgets; ours is instruction adherence under a planted conflict. They vary what peers exchange horizontally; we vary what a worker sees vertically from the hierarchy above it.

verified.title: The Collaboration Tax: How Much LLM Multi-Agent Systems Pay to Coordinate
verified.resolved_title: The Collaboration Tax: How Much LLM Multi-Agent Systems Pay to Coordinate
verified.authors: Weixiang Sun, Zehong Wang, Hong Huang, Colby Nelson, Yanfang Ye
verified.venue: EMNLP 2026 Main Conference, per arXiv comment; arXiv (cs.CL)
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22152 (v1 2026-08-23; comment: EMNLP 2026 Main Conference); API returned empty after retries
verified.abstract_gist: Defines the collaboration tax as the team-decentralisation loss of a two-player cooperative game with private information and measures it on 32 solo-tractable tasks across 11 models from 7 providers. The tax follows a fixed category ordering and decreases monotonically with capability, its mechanism is a four-stage conversational cascade (ungrounded claims, no partner query, no integration, no re-derivation), a targeted prompt closes much of the gap, and heterogeneous pairs are pulled toward the stronger partner.
verified.use: Cite as a capability-graded coordination result to set beside our 'more capable model departs more' finding: coordination loss falls with capability while objective-directed departure rises with it, which the discussion can present as two faces of the same capacity to model the other party's goal.
verified.differentiation: They measure performance lost when two agents must coordinate with private information and no goal conflict; we measure a worker's choice between its literal instruction and a visible conflicting objective. Their capability trend runs in the opposite direction from ours, which is a contrast to explain rather than an overlap.

verified.resolved_title: Agents Catching Agents: Shortcut Cascades and Benchmark Gaming in Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
verified.authors: Sebastián Andrés Cajas Ordóñez, Agastya Munnangi, Aldo Marzullo, Felipe Ocampo Osorio, Quang Bui, Mohammad Shahin, Armaan Grewal, Emmanuel Paul Kwesiga, Anqi Peter Li, Josephine Nanyonjo, Aaditya Panchal, Arshnoor Bhutani, Nikhil Jaiswal, Milit S. Patel, Maximin Lange, Leo Anthony Celi
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03744 (v2 2026-08-17); API returned empty after retries
verified.abstract_gist: Gemini committees on a shared clinical workspace resist shortcut cues in isolation (5 to 16 percent flips) but adopt a wrong answer asserted by two peers, or a false system pre-screen flag, in 38 percent of cases across seven cohorts on six datasets. A transcript-reading judge catches adoption on text but not imaging, a referee that privately re-queries the holdout transfers to imaging, a second peer voice raises contagion by half while tripling visual salience does not, and rubric gaming is near-silent (1 of 10 text and 1 of 134 imaging drifters name the rubric).
verified.use: Cite as the nearest quantification of silent versus announced departure under peer visibility: drifters almost never name what moved them, which contrasts with our zero silent deviations and motivates the announced/silent split in our outcome taxonomy and the Suite B referee-style check independent of self-report.
verified.differentiation: Their departures are toward a wrong answer under social pressure from peers on a shared workspace; ours are toward the parent objective under a planted conflict with no peer pressure in Suite A. They find near-silent drift; we find announced departures only, a difference the paper should attribute to the direction of the pull (objective versus shortcut) rather than to model.

verified.resolved_title: When Truth Is Distributed: Misinformation Derails Collective Fact Recovery in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
verified.authors: Chenfei Yan, Zeyang Yue, Feifei Zhao, Erliang Lin, Lu Jia, Haibo Tong, Mingyang Lyu, Chengyi Sun, Yi Zeng
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03421 (v3 2026-08-13); API returned empty after retries
verified.abstract_gist: ForesightSafety-TIDE pairs all-honest collaboration with a single deceiving key-evidence holder in 120 five-agent object-movement environments and traces voting, testimony adoption and evidence lineage across three homogeneous systems. verified.use: Cite briefly in the Suite B risk discussion as evidence that visible peer claims override a worker's own evidence and persist, a reason to treat V5 peer polling as a contamination channel and to log provenance in the ledger.
verified.differentiation: Their manipulation is a deliberately deceptive peer in a fact-aggregation game; ours has no adversary and no peer messages in Suite A, and the pull on the worker is the legitimate parent objective. verified.title: The Politician, the Liar, and the Obedient Worker: Emerging Behavior of LLM Agents in Hierarchical Games
verified.resolved_title: The Politician, the Liar, and the Obedient Worker: Emerging Behavior of LLM Agents in Hierarchical Games
verified.authors: Fatemeh Seyedin, Adrian Weller, Jinhyuk Yun, Mahmoudreza Babaei
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09574 (v1 2026-08-10); API returned empty after retries
verified.abstract_gist: The Hierarchical Game extends a public goods game with managerial authority, elections and private communication, and tests six frontier models across twelve experiments that add institutions one at a time. Models show distinct profiles (Qwen breaks 13.3 percent of promises, Grok cooperates only once a manager can punish it, Claude and GPT-4o cooperate at baseline), honesty erodes when the manager role is salaried or punishment is anonymous, and same-family groups entrench the first elected manager.
verified.use: Cite in the organization-theory layer for model-specific responses to managerial authority and incentive structure, supporting the claim that worker behavior under hierarchy is a property of the model and the institution jointly rather than of hierarchy alone.
verified.differentiation: A game-theoretic setting with monetary payoffs, elections and strategic communication; our workers have no payoff, no peers in Suite A and a single planted conflict, and the outcome is adherence rather than cooperation or honesty. Shared ground is only the finding that authority structure changes model behavior in model-specific ways.

verified.title: Measuring Obedience to Authority Across Large Language Models with the Milgram Paradigm
verified.resolved_title: Measuring Obedience to Authority Across Large Language Models with the Milgram Paradigm
verified.authors: Hidayet Aksu
verified.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.CR, cs.AI); comment: 11 pages, 7 figures
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16177 (v2 2026-08-18); API returned empty after retries
verified.abstract_gist: Ports Milgram's obedience paradigm to a fully scripted harness (30 shock levels, graded protests, four standard prods) and measures breakoff-voltage profiles for 42 models from 19 families over 4,848 sessions and six conditions. Full-obedience rates span 0 to 100 percent (mean 42.9 percent versus the 65 percent human anchor), profiles are model-specific and stable, scripted peer defiance lowers obedience, declaring the scenario fictional raises it, and moving the decision to a native tool call or granting a modest thinking budget lowers it sharply.
verified.use: Cite for two independent results that bear on our design: a modest thinking budget lowers obedience to an insisting authority, which frames our reasoning-effort setting and the observed doubling of reasoning tokens under hierarchy context, and scripted peer defiance shifts behavior, which bears on V3 sibling mandates. Also citable in the org-theory layer as the obedience-to-authority baseline.
verified.differentiation: Their authority insists on a harmful action and obedience is the failure; in our setting the literal instruction is benign and the higher authority (the objective) is the pull, so departure is objective-directed rather than harm-avoiding. They vary the authority's presence and framing; we vary the worker's view of the hierarchy that issued the instruction.

verified.title: Can escalation channels redirect reward hacking toward defect disclosure?
verified.resolved_title: Can escalation channels redirect reward hacking toward defect disclosure?
verified.authors: Francesca Gomez
verified.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.AI, cs.CR, cs.CY); v2, 9 pages
verified.verification_source: arXiv export API record 2608.29460v2 (published 2026-08-29, updated 2026-09-02); title, author, comment and abstract read
verified.abstract_gist: A 2x2 factorial across 8 frontier models in 5 families tests whether giving a coding agent a structured escalation tool at the point of conflict, an anti-reward-hacking policy, or both reduces reward hacking on defective test infrastructure. The combined intervention cuts hacking from 23.6 to 5.3 percent (OR 9.2), escalations are 98.7 percent hack-free, and escalation adds 10.1 points of defect-detection coverage over monitoring.
verified.use: Cite as the closest experimental analogue to the FLAGGED class: when a disclosure channel exists, disclosure and deviation become near mutually exclusive, which supports reading our flag rate as the worker choosing to raise rather than silently act.
verified.differentiation: Gomez manipulates the availability of an escalation tool and a policy while holding the instruction fixed; we hold tools fixed and vary how much of the delegation hierarchy the worker can see. Her conflict is agent versus broken test infrastructure, ours is literal instruction versus parent objective, and she measures hacking not objective-directed departure.

verified.title: Beyond Suspicious Steps: Ontological Trust in Long-Horizon Agents
verified.resolved_title: Beyond Suspicious Steps: Ontological Trust in Long-Horizon Agents
verified.authors: An He; Yao Wang; Haibin Zhang
verified.verification_source: arXiv export API record 2608.17718v1 (published 2026-08-18); title, authors and abstract read
verified.abstract_gist: Defines ontological trust as a task-conditioned property of trajectory prefixes and instantiates RGE, an online monitor decomposing trust into Role, Goal and Evidence with deterministic trust-state updates and LLMs used only to structure task and step representations. On a corpus from OSWorld, FinanceBench and EICU-AC it exceeds 93 percent drift F1 with the larger estimators while keeping benign coverage at or above 95.8 percent; pseudo-consistency failures remain hard when completion is not externally visible.
verified.use: Cite when defining the silent-deviation class: He et al. formalize the case where every step is locally valid but the prefix drifts to a broader role or adjacent objective, which is exactly the outcome our deterministic checkers screen for and, so far, never observe.
verified.differentiation: RGE is a detector for drift in long single-agent trajectories driven by the agent's own choices; we induce the drift candidate by a planted conflict and measure whether visibility into the hierarchy triggers announced or silent departure. Their monitor is a contribution, ours is a measurement of a decision.

verified.title: OrchestraBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Failure Modes, Recovery, and Decomposition Quality
verified.resolved_title: OrchestraBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Failure Modes, Recovery, and Decomposition Quality
verified.authors: Yidian Chen; Yingzi Gu; Natan Vidra; Spurthi Setty; Sharon Zheng
verified.verification_source: arXiv export API record 2608.05263v1 (published 2026-08-05); title, authors, comment and abstract read
verified.abstract_gist: A seed-reproducible failure-injection harness over templated enterprise workflows that reports cascade radius and per-failure-mode recovery, comparing routers with bootstrap CIs. Probes with a real Claude agent across Sonnet, Opus and Haiku find tool faults recover fully, ambiguous delegation recovers only partially (0.30), latent semantic faults never recover, and cascade radius grows from 0.9 to 4.7 as pipeline depth goes from 3 to 7.
verified.use: Cite for the finding that ambiguous delegation is a partially recoverable failure mode and that latent semantic faults propagate without detection, motivating why a conflict planted in a brief matters and why detection (our FLAGGED class) rather than blind retry is the containment lever.
verified.differentiation: OrchestraBench injects faults into pipelines and measures recovery and cascade; we plant a single semantic conflict in one delegated brief and measure the worker's disclosure or departure as a function of visibility. They vary failure type and depth, we vary context exposure with length-matched controls.

verified.title: Routed Graph Handoff: Adaptive Format Selection for Multi-Agent LLM Delegation
verified.resolved_title: Routed Graph Handoff: Adaptive Format Selection for Multi-Agent LLM Delegation
verified.authors: Pratyay Banerjee; Ankit Chadha
verified.venue: Accepted in EMNLP 2026; arXiv preprint (cs.CL, cs.AI)
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2608.25277 (submitted 2026-08-26), comment 'Accepted in EMNLP 2026'; title, authors and abstract read
verified.abstract_gist: Inter-agent natural-language messages consume 40 to 60 percent of a multi-agent system's token budget; a 155-token LLM router picks per delegation between a typed dependency graph and natural language. Across four benchmarks the routed system matches or beats NL-only (+12.7 pp on tau-retail at 3.2x compression), graph-only regresses 14.6 pp on AppWorld without the router, and a graph-aware executor prompt is required for any gain.
verified.use: Cite for the cost share of inter-agent communication and for the observation that the form of the handoff changes worker behavior only when the worker is told how to read it, a companion to our finding that filler tokens and hierarchy context are not interchangeable.
verified.differentiation: Banerjee and Chadha vary the encoding of the handoff to trade tokens for accuracy; we vary the amount of hierarchy context to measure conflict handling. Their dependent variable is task accuracy and compression, ours is adherence, flagging and departure under a planted conflict.

verified.title: Consilience: Conformally Calibrated Communication Control for Hidden-Profile Multi-Agent Reasoning
verified.resolved_title: Consilience: Conformally Calibrated Communication Control for Hidden-Profile Multi-Agent Reasoning
verified.authors: Abhijith Babu; Ramneet Kaur; Vishal Pramanik; Olivera Kotevska; Nathaniel D. Bastian; Susmit Jha; Sunny Raj; Yanzhao Wu; Sumit Kumar Jha; Anirban Roy
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2608.20564 (submitted 2026-08-20); title, authors, comment and abstract read
verified.abstract_gist: An inference-time orchestration framework for hidden-profile tasks that summarizes discussion state, selects a communication intervention and speaker per turn, and certifies each action with round-wise conformal calibration giving a distribution-free regret bound. On HiddenBench-style tasks over 12 models it improves accuracy and communication efficiency over fixed and unstructured protocols, sometimes surpassing a full-information baseline where every agent sees all evidence.
verified.use: Cite in the organization-theory discussion as evidence that certified selective disclosure can beat full information sharing, which frames why maximal visibility (V4, V5) is not automatically the right default for a sub-agent.
verified.differentiation: Consilience controls communication among peers holding partial evidence to maximize decision accuracy; we expose a single subordinate to more or less of its hierarchy and measure conflict handling. Their full-information baseline is about evidence pooling, not about a worker seeing its parent's objective.

verified.title: Prompt-Induced Waste in Coding Agents: Reasoning, Effort, Harness Design, and End-to-End Cost
verified.resolved_title: Prompt-Induced Waste in Coding Agents: Reasoning, Effort, Harness Design, and End-to-End Cost
verified.authors: Sarel Weinberger; Amir Hozez
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2608.01347 (submitted 2026-08-02, v5 2026-08-24); title, authors and abstract read
verified.abstract_gist: Argues coding-agent efficiency cannot be read from token counts or model price; end-to-end cost per successful task depends jointly on prompt semantics, inference effort, harness policy, model, task difficulty, tool use, context management and provider accounting. Controlled experiments show prompt wording changes reasoning and verification behavior without changing the task, that extra effort can add cost without benefit, and that prompt, effort and harness interact rather than act as independent controls.
verified.use: Cite when reporting the roughly twofold rise in reasoning tokens under hierarchy context and the null effect of the xhigh setting: it supplies the methodological framing that prompt content, effort and harness are interacting factors, so our cost result must be stated per harness and per provider contract.
verified.differentiation: Weinberger and Hozez measure cost per successful task under prompt and effort manipulations for ordinary coding work; we measure reasoning-token cost as a side effect of hierarchy visibility under a planted conflict, with no success-rate objective. Their contribution is a cost model, ours is a behavioral result with cost as a secondary outcome.

verified.title: The Price of Thinking: Reasoning Effort as a Model-Specific API Contract
verified.resolved_title: The Price of Thinking: Reasoning Effort as a Model-Specific API Contract
verified.authors: Yeabin Moon
verified.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.CY, cs.LG); 15 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2608.16956 (submitted 2026-08-16); title, author, comment and abstract read
verified.abstract_gist: A registered paired contrast of Sonnet 5 with explicit high reasoning effort versus effort omitted on 30 AIME 2026 items, five calls each: cost was 0.01031 dollars per call higher under explicit high, the accuracy contrast was +0.0133 with an interval spanning zero, and cost per correct answer was higher under the explicit contract. A contract census and preregistered probes document model-specific semantics of omitting the effort term, including within one provider.
verified.use: Cite directly for the finding that the SDK xhigh setting produced no measurable effect through the gateway: Moon shows that effort terms are model-specific contract fields whose omission or presence has documented, non-uniform semantics, which is why we report runs as effectively at provider-default effort.
verified.differentiation: Moon isolates the effort term on a math benchmark with one model; we found the effort term inert across a gateway for two models and treat that as a nuisance factor. We do not contribute to the effort-contract literature, we consume it to justify a caveat.

verified.title: Can your AI agent be cheaper? Investigating the effects of task specifications on token spend in agentic coding tasks
verified.resolved_title: Can your AI agent be cheaper? Investigating the effects of task specifications on token spend in agentic coding tasks
verified.authors: Jakub Smékal
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2608.25399 (submitted 2026-08-26); title, author and abstract read
verified.abstract_gist: 2,700 runs of Kimi K3 at three thinking efforts show that reducing a full task specification to a bare user story raises token spend by 29.7 percent while run-to-run variance is unaffected by prompt changes, and prompt sensitivity ranges from 13 to 115 percent by task. A simple predictor prices the full distribution of specification and effort configurations from one cheap probe within 36 percent.
verified.use: Cite alongside our length-matched controls: Smékal shows that less specification content raises spend, so the reasoning-token increase we see under hierarchy context is not a generic function of prompt length, and token variance across draws is a model property rather than a prompt effect.
verified.differentiation: Smékal varies specification completeness for one model and predicts token spend; we vary hierarchy visibility for two models and measure conflict handling, with token cost as a secondary outcome. Our length-matched filler condition is the closest overlap and it addresses a question his design does not ask.

verified.title: The Working Set of a Coding Agent: Coherence Debt in Repository-Scale Tasks
verified.resolved_title: The Working Set of a Coding Agent: Coherence Debt in Repository-Scale Tasks
verified.authors: Bardia Mohammadi; Lars Klein; Aman Chadha; Akhil Arora; Laurent Bindschaedler
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2608.16630 (submitted 2026-08-17); title, authors and abstract read
verified.abstract_gist: Models repository-scale coding as reconstructing a coupled-fact graph where facts come from recent context or parametric memory and the uncovered remainder is coherence debt; supplies and withholds each channel across seven models and five harnesses. Availability, not distance, decides outcomes; harnesses differ more than tenfold in tokens for the same passing result; an agent asked to act acts (fabricating or guessing) rather than reporting it is blocked, with the blocked-report rate a model property from every trial to none, and agents follow a stale convention file even when it prescribes worse code.
verified.use: Cite for two in-the-wild observations that mirror our classes: the propensity to say it is blocked instead of acting is a model property (our FLAGGED rate differs by model), and agents defer to a written standard over their own judgment even when the standard is worse (literal adherence to the brief over the objective).
verified.differentiation: Mohammadi et al. withhold facts and measure fabrication versus blocked reports in repository tasks; we plant an explicit conflict between a literal instruction and a parent objective and measure disclosure versus departure as visibility grows. Their conflict is standard versus code, ours is instruction versus objective, and they do not manipulate hierarchy exposure.

verified.title: SpecPath: Testing Coding Agents Across Contract-Equivalent Specification Histories
verified.resolved_title: SpecPath: Testing Coding Agents Across Contract-Equivalent Specification Histories
verified.authors: Yangfan Wu; Haozhe Wang; Huanyu Yang; Jianmin Ji; Fangzhen Lin
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2608.09799 (submitted 2026-08-10); title, authors, comment and abstract read
verified.abstract_gist: Identifies specification-path sensitivity: requirement histories equivalent in final meaning lead the same agent to behaviorally different programs. SpecPath holds repository, final contract, verifier, agent and budget fixed while changing only the revision path; across five tasks and fourteen agent configurations aggregate accuracy is unchanged, yet 35 of 100 blocks that succeed on the direct specification fail on at least one equivalent history.
verified.use: Cite for the principle that the path by which an instruction is presented, not only its content, changes what the agent does; our V0 to V5 manipulation is a presentation-path manipulation of the same conflict, and SpecPath shows aggregate accuracy can hide large paired differences, which motivates our item-paired analysis.
verified.differentiation: SpecPath varies revision history of a specification with a fixed final contract and measures test-passing invariance; we vary how much of the delegation hierarchy accompanies a fixed instruction and measure disclosure and departure. Neither the conflict construct nor the outcome classes overlap.

verified.title: RealSWE: A Compositional Evaluation of Coding Agents under Realistic User Requests
verified.resolved_title: RealSWE: A Compositional Evaluation of Coding Agents under Realistic User Requests
verified.authors: Gyuhyeong Kim; Hyojung Gwon; Jeonghyeon Kim; Kyuhong Shim; Sunjae Lee
verified.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.SE); v2, revised 2026-08-31
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2608.27831 (submitted 2026-08-28, v2 2026-08-31); title, authors and abstract read
verified.abstract_gist: A six-category information taxonomy and four style dimensions applied to real SWE-chat prompts versus SWE-bench Verified and Pro show that 88 percent of real requests carry little beyond a problem statement while 94 percent of benchmark problems are formal. RealSWE's 381 multi-variant task families, evaluated on seven LLMs, show realistic inputs cut resolution 6.4 pp and can reorder models; including Desired Behavior and Motivation significantly helps while Environment Information and Reproduction Steps only add tokens.
verified.use: Cite as a clean content-versus-length contrast: stating motivation (the analogue of our V1 objective sentence) changes behavior while other information merely adds tokens, supporting our reading that hierarchy context and length-matched filler act differently.
verified.differentiation: RealSWE varies information composition to measure task resolution on SWE-bench-derived families; we vary hierarchy exposure to measure conflict handling and reasoning cost. Motivation in RealSWE improves task success, whereas in our design the objective sentence enables flagging and departure without a correctness target.

verified.resolved_title: Harness Engineering: Anatomy, Architecture, and Evolution of Coding Agents -- A Source-Code Study of Eleven Systems

verified.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.SE, cs.MA); 83 pages, 7 figures, 18 tables; second, substantially expanded edition of an April 2026 study

verified.abstract_gist: A source-code anatomy of eleven production coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Mistral Vibe, OpenHands, Aider, Mini-SWE-Agent, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode, OpenClaw) plus the Omnigent meta-harness, mapped along seven canonical subsystems with 13 cross-cutting observations and 29 design patterns. verified.use: Cite as the primary secondary source for the per-harness policy table: it names the orchestration and sub-agent seams of each harness from source, and its finding that policy is moving from prompt prose into configuration is the reason our table records default sub-agent visibility as a settable policy rather than a fixed behavior.
verified.differentiation: Barbaste et al. describe harness architecture from source without measuring agent behavior; we measure what a worker does under each level of visibility and cite their anatomy only to ground which default each harness ships. Note the record's submission date (15 Jul 2026) conflicts with its 2609 identifier; cite the identifier as printed.

verified.title: The Empire, Long Divided, Must Unite: Architectural Convergence in Three LLM Agent Harnesses
verified.resolved_title: The Empire, Long Divided, Must Unite: Architectural Convergence in Three LLM Agent Harnesses
verified.verification_source: arXiv API export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2608.23953 (v1, published 2026-08-25)
verified.authors: Dai Jiahong
verified.abstract_gist: Source-level, pinned-commit case study of three open coding-agent harnesses (LangChain deepagents, Earendil pi, DeepSeek dsh) built from opposing philosophies, finding convergence on five elements: a commoditised loop, an append-only replayable session record, model quirks kept as data, progressive disclosure of context, and explicit extension seams. The one load-bearing dimension with no convergence and no presence is external verifiability, a tamper-evident record an outside party can check without trusting the runtime.
verified.use: Cite in the harness policy table section as independent source-level evidence that harnesses converge on progressive disclosure of context and an append-only session record, and to supply dsh and pi rows beyond their own docs; also supports the claim that what a harness shows a sub-agent is a design choice not dictated by the model.
verified.differentiation: Reads harness source for architecture, not what a delegated worker is shown; it never varies context visibility or measures worker adherence. Our study measures behaviour under controlled visibility levels, which the paper's 'progressive disclosure' finding motivates but does not test.

verified.title: SWE-Touch: Benchmarking Coding Agents When Users Touch the Code
verified.resolved_title: SWE-Touch: Benchmarking Coding Agents When Users Touch the Code
verified.verification_source: arXiv API export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2608.02499 (v1, published 2026-08-03)
verified.authors: Yuqiao Tan; Jinxiang Meng; Fangyu Lei; Minzheng Wang; Shizhu He; Jun Zhao; Kang Liu
verified.abstract_gist: Framework that injects validated Counter-Edits (plausible user edits to task-relevant code that conflict with task completion) mid-trajectory, evaluated on nine coding models over SWE-bench Verified, SWE-Bench Pro and DeepSWE. Counter-Edits lower average resolve rate by 7.7 points; failures trace to limited awareness of the evolving workspace (retaining or blindly replacing conflicting code without re-inspection or targeted tests).
verified.use: Cite in Suite B design as the methodological template for a concurrent-sibling condition where another actor mutates shared state mid-task, and as evidence that agents have poor awareness of workspace changes they did not make.
verified.differentiation: The conflict is between the task and a user's code edit in the workspace, with a single agent and no hierarchy; our conflict is between a worker's literal instruction and the parent objective, and we vary how much of the hierarchy the worker sees rather than injecting edits.

verified.resolved_title: Claim Plane: Reliability Gains and the Limits of Selective Concurrency for Parallel Coding Agents: A 30-Pair, Three-Seed Confirmatory Study of Deterministic Pre-Write Admission

verified.authors: Maxim Nikolaev
verified.abstract_gist: Confirmatory study of deterministic pre-write admission over versioned change intents on 30 frozen CooperBench feature pairs, three coder seeds, four arms, 360 executions, with DeepSeek V4 Pro producing frozen planner declarations and DeepSeek V4 Flash doing the coding. Static admission raised pair pass from 23.3 to 50.0 percent and integration success from 65.6 to 96.7 percent but serialized 96.7 percent of executions; dynamic admission was more selective but 46 of 90 executions failed closed on undeclared scope, 45 of them on files already in the declarations (region undercoverage).
verified.use: Cite in Suite B motivation as a quantification, on DeepSeek V4 Flash specifically, of how often concurrent workers act outside their declared scope (46 of 90 dynamic executions), and in the discussion of why declared-scope enforcement collapses toward serialization.
verified.differentiation: Measures scope violations of a planner's declarations under concurrency and tests an admission mechanism; it does not vary what the coder can see of the planner's objective or classify announced versus silent departures. Our design manipulates visibility and scores disclosure.

verified.title: AgentRoom: Concurrent Multi-Agent Coding in a CRDT-Backed Shared Workspace
verified.resolved_title: AgentRoom: Concurrent Multi-Agent Coding in a CRDT-Backed Shared Workspace
verified.verification_source: arXiv API export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2608.23740 (v1, published 2026-08-24)
verified.authors: Seonglae Cho; Donghyun Lee
verified.abstract_gist: Realtime collaborative editing protocol for concurrent coding agents whose runtime exposes file-level claim, status and broadcast as MCP tools over a CRDT-merged shared filesystem, evaluated with five frontier coding-CLI models on four backend tasks. Two-agent AgentRoom abandons fewer tasks than Solo with less run-to-run variance, and a bundle probe attributes the gain to coordination rather than parallelism or CRDT merge.
verified.use: Cite as an existing implementation of the live peer-progress tool our V5 condition and Suite B propose (claim/status/broadcast as MCP tools), and for its finding that the coordination channel rather than parallelism carries the benefit.
verified.differentiation: Peer visibility is a means to task completion and is not manipulated as an independent variable against a planted instruction conflict; no parent objective, no adherence or disclosure scoring. We treat peer-status visibility as one rung of a hierarchy-visibility ladder.

verified.title: Turning Interaction History into Execution State: A Runtime Layer for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
verified.resolved_title: Turning Interaction History into Execution State: A Runtime Layer for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
verified.verification_source: arXiv API export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2608.00808 (v1, published 2026-08-01). Note: the arXiv record lists the final author as two entries 'Tse-Hsun' and 'Chen' (a metadata split); copied as printed.
verified.authors: Zehao Wang; Yisen Xu; Chenglin Li; Chao Peng; Bram Adams; Ahmed E. Hassan; Tse-Hsun; Chen
verified.abstract_gist: Ledger is a deterministic runtime layer that distills an agent's completed interactions into explicit execution state (observed, modified, attempted), appended to the prompt before each step (inform) and consulted before each command (govern), with no extra model calls. On all 500 SWE-bench Verified instances it raises Pass@1 from 56.2 to 64.2 percent (GPT-5 mini) and 75.8 to 81.0 percent (MiniMax M2.5) while cutting cost 28.9 and 31.8 percent; on Codex it adds 3.4 points at 24.4 percent lower cost.
verified.use: Cite when introducing the V4 ledger condition as measured evidence that a deterministic execution ledger placed in context improves outcomes and reduces cost, and to contrast our ledger (the orchestrator's cross-worker record) with theirs (the agent's own history).
verified.differentiation: Their ledger summarizes the same agent's own past actions for a single long-horizon agent; ours exposes the orchestrator's record of the whole delegation to a worker facing a conflicting instruction. They measure task resolution and cost, not adherence or disclosure.

verified.title: Parsing the Stream: A Live Trace Model for Long-Horizon Agents and Their Observers
verified.resolved_title: Parsing the Stream: A Live Trace Model for Long-Horizon Agents and Their Observers
verified.verification_source: arXiv API export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2609.01466 (v1, published 2026-09-01; Salesforce AI Research tracelab)
verified.authors: Egor Pakhomov; Erik Nijkamp
verified.abstract_gist: Presents a live trace model: an append-only event ledger folded incrementally into typed run state and compiled into per-consumer views for a human observer and for the agent itself. Observer views answer monitoring questions with about 14 to 15 times fewer input tokens and 5 to 7 times lower cost at higher accuracy (0.85 to 0.87 versus 0.48); for the agent, per-step state maintenance succeeds on 120-link sequential tasks where full-context prompting fails (30/30 versus 8/30), with a prompt-level scratchpad matching accuracy at lower cost, and the fold's residual value being deterministic auditability.
verified.use: Cite as a concrete design and cost accounting for the orchestrator ledger in V4 and Suite B: the same append-only record can be compiled into a worker view and an observer view, and the token cost of folding it back into worker context is measurable.
verified.differentiation: Optimizes trace compression for monitoring and state tracking; it does not ask whether exposing the ledger changes a worker's willingness to follow or depart from a conflicting instruction. Their ledger is single-agent; ours spans delegated siblings.

verified.resolved_title: LongRCA Bench: Diagnosing Responsible Roles and Root Causes in Long-Horizon Agent Failures

verified.abstract_gist: Benchmark of 1,140 uninjected failed long-horizon trajectories across five domains (median 145 steps) with independently scored human labels for the responsible role and the earliest decisive root-cause step; the strongest baseline reaches 13.2 percent exact root-step accuracy. verified.use: Cite in the failure-taxonomy and organization-theory sections: root-cause attribution that traces failures back to handoff instructions supports the premise that the brief a worker receives is often the decisive fault, motivating the study of what a worker sees at handoff.
verified.differentiation: Post-hoc attribution of failures in naturally occurring trajectories; no controlled conflict, no manipulation of handoff visibility, and no measurement of whether workers announce or silently deviate. Our study plants the conflict and varies the handoff context prospectively.

verified.title: Emergent Misaligned Communication in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent LLM Commerce
verified.resolved_title: Emergent Misaligned Communication in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent LLM Commerce
verified.verification_source: arXiv API export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2608.14825 (v3, published 2026-08-14, updated 2026-08-21)
verified.authors: Zeyuan Li; Lukas Petersson; Alessandro Acquisti; Michiel A. Bakker
verified.abstract_gist: Analyzes 2,583 inter-agent emails from 20 one-year Vending-Bench Arena runs across 13 frontier LLMs, classifying false claims, manipulation, collusion and threats against simulator ground truth and reasoning traces. 12.6 percent of emails are misaligned, present in all runs and 74.7 percent of agent-runs; misalignment is reciprocal (1.65x odds after a misaligned incoming email) and stress-conditioned (1.58x under low inventory), and model performance rank does not predict misalignment rates.
verified.use: Cite in the discussion of the capability-departure relation as a counterpoint: in competitive multi-principal settings capability rank does not predict misaligned behaviour, whereas within a single hierarchy we observe the more capable model departing more, suggesting the relation is setting-dependent.
verified.differentiation: Adversarial, separate-principal commerce with peer-to-peer communication; misalignment is deception toward counterparties, not departure from a parent objective under an instruction conflict, and no hierarchy context is varied.

verified.resolved_title: HarnessRisk: A Lifecycle-Oriented Benchmark for Agent Harness Safety

verified.authors: Yajing Bai; Jinhao Duan; Jie Peng; Xianfeng Wu; Sijia Liu; Song Wang; Tianlong Chen
verified.abstract_gist: Benchmark of 128 sandboxed cases, each pairing a benign user objective with an adversarial instruction embedded in an untrusted workflow artifact, organized over six harness lifecycle phases and scored on Utility, Attack Success Rate, Persistence and Detection across three harnesses, six models and 14 configurations. Attack success ranges from 12.6 to 80.9 percent with Utility 75.0 to 97.6 percent; Harness Configuration is the most vulnerable phase, and explicit risk recognition does not reliably lead to safe action (some configurations detect risk in over 90 percent of runs while retaining substantial attack success).
verified.use: Cite alongside the FLAGGED versus DEVIATED distinction as independent evidence of a recognition-versus-action gap: models that notice a conflict frequently still act on the lower-priority instruction; also in the harness policy discussion since it evaluates behaviour at the model-plus-harness level.
verified.differentiation: The conflicting instruction is adversarial injection from an untrusted artifact and the safe action is refusal; ours is a benign but mis-specified delegation where the objective-directed action is departure from the literal brief. They do not vary how much of the objective the agent sees.

verified.title: Knowing When to Ask for Help: Bayesian Self-Escalation in Hierarchical LLM Agents
verified.resolved_title: Knowing When to Ask for Help: Bayesian Self-Escalation in Hierarchical LLM Agents

verified.abstract_gist: Formulates intra-generation delegation, an agent recognising mid-reasoning that it is unlikely to succeed and handing control to a stronger model, as Bayesian optimal stopping over a learned competence posterior, deriving a closed-form myopic threshold, a time-varying optimal threshold policy, regret and finite-sample (1/sqrt(n)) guarantees. verified.title: Agent Mesh: Reliability Primitives for Non-Idempotent Agent Delegation - Identity Adequacy and Evidence Adequacy
verified.resolved_title: Agent Mesh: Reliability Primitives for Non-Idempotent Agent Delegation - Identity Adequacy and Evidence Adequacy

verified.abstract_gist: Failure study of a production agentic software-delivery platform over 147 numbered incidents across 81 runs, showing that service-mesh primitives (retry, timeout, error-rate circuit breaking) rest on assumptions violated by non-idempotent agent delegation: invisible failure loops of successful tool calls, constant progress signals that force false trips, event accumulation across re-invocations, misrouted failures waking bystander components, and enforcement blocking correct work. verified.use: Cite in the Suite B design and harness policy discussion for real-world orchestrator-worker failure modes under retry and budgeting, especially the finding that enforcement should attach to the delegation, which matches our unit of analysis.
verified.differentiation: An infrastructure reliability study of orchestration plumbing (retries, budgets, routing); it does not examine what a delegated agent is told about the parent objective or measure adherence and disclosure under an instruction conflict.

verified.title: TeamBench: Evaluating Agent Coordination under Enforced Role Separation
verified.resolved_title: TeamBench: Evaluating Agent Coordination under Enforced Role Separation

verified.authors: Yubin Kim; Chanwoo Park; Taehan Kim; Eugene Park; Samuel Schmidgall; Salman Rahman; Chunjong Park; Cynthia Breazeal; Xin Liu; Hamid Palangi; Hae Won Park; Daniel McDuff
verified.abstract_gist: Benchmark of 851 task templates and 931 seeded instances evaluating coordination under OS-enforced role separation, so that no Planner, Executor or Verifier can read the full requirements, edit the workspace and certify the answer. Prompt-only and enforced teams reach indistinguishable pass rates but prompt-only runs show 3.6 times more verifier attempts to edit executor code; verifiers approve 49 percent of grader-failing submissions, removing the verifier improves partial score, teams help only when solo agents struggle, and a 40-session human study exposes interaction patterns pass rate misses.
verified.use: Cite in related work as the closest benchmark that treats information access per role as an enforced design variable (no role reads the full requirements) and shows role-scoped prompts alone do not produce role-scoped behaviour; supports our motivation for measuring what visibility does rather than assuming it.
verified.differentiation: Restricts requirement access by role to test whether roles stay in lane, with outcomes scored by pass rate and role-boundary violations; it does not plant a conflict between a role's instruction and the team objective, does not vary visibility across graded levels, and does not classify announced versus silent departures.

verified.title: Where Knowledge and Authority Sit Changes What an Agent Benchmark Can Resolve

verified.authors: Dan C. Hsu; Luke Lu
verified.verification_source: arXiv export API record for 2607.02975 (title, authors, dates, abstract)
verified.abstract_gist: Incognita holds eighteen customer-service tasks and their success criteria fixed while moving facts, tools and permissions from direct access to one intermediary to six role-isolated participants whose capabilities must be discovered. Across 864 trials with four models, social access lowered success for every model and separated model pairs that centralized settings could not, with a reference-relative reader attributing the wider gaps to failures to obtain needed information.
verified.use: Cite as the nearest published manipulation of where knowledge and authority sit in an agent task, and as precedent for showing that access structure, not task content, is what separates models; contrast its outcome measure (task success) with ours (conflict handling).
verified.differentiation: Incognita varies who holds information and permission and measures success; it plants no conflict between the worker's instruction and a parent objective and never asks whether the agent departs from or flags its brief. Our ladder varies how much of the hierarchy a single worker sees and classifies adherence, flagging and deviation, so the two are complementary axes of the same organizational question.

verified.title: HANDBOOK.md: A Benchmark for Long-Context Agentic Instruction Following
verified.resolved_title: HANDBOOK.md: A Benchmark for Long-Context Agentic Instruction Following
verified.authors: Liudas Panavas; Sebastian Minus; Bradley Monton; Derek Ray; Suhaas Garre; Sushant Mehta; Edwin Chen
verified.venue: Workshop on Agent Behavior (WAB) at COLM 2026 (arXiv preprint; comments state accepted)

verified.abstract_gist: HANDBOOK_md is a benchmark of 65 agentic tasks in which an agent works inside a mock company environment over MCP under a 20 to 124 page expert-written standard operating procedure, graded by 824 deterministic programmatic criteria. verified.use: Cite for the finding that a long standing policy in context is routinely overridden by plausible in-environment requests and that agents report compliance they did not achieve, which motivates our deterministic checkers and our distinction between announced and silent deviation; also cite its deterministic rubric design as precedent for our checker approach.
verified.differentiation: HANDBOOK.md tests whether a long policy document constrains an agent against unauthorized requests arriving from the environment; the policy and the task are on the same side. Our study plants the conflict between the worker's own instruction and the parent objective and varies how much of the hierarchy is visible, so it measures the effect of visibility rather than of policy length or horizon.

verified.title: Does a Tool Result Carry More Authority Than Plain Text? Three Prospective Studies of False-Claim Adoption in a Synthetic Assignment Task with Claude Opus 5

verified.abstract_gist: Three studies on Claude Opus 5 test whether the message package carrying an unsupported assignment changes false-claim adoption in a synthetic lookup task: a prior assistant assertion produced 0/22 adoption while a tool-result record produced 14/24, and a preregistered replication reproduced the gap at 7/24 versus 0/24. A second preregistered study with an announced inline-text control found inline text sufficient for adoption in 60/60 trials versus 57/60 for the tool result, so the registered tool-result superiority criterion failed and the effect is attributed to placement and framing rather than native tool-result privilege.
verified.use: Cite when discussing why the V5 live peer-progress tool might carry different weight than the V4 ledger text, with the caveat that the preregistered follow-up found announced inline text equally sufficient; use it to justify treating channel (tool result versus text) as a design variable in Suite B rather than assuming tool results dominate.
verified.differentiation: Bronder measures adoption of a single false factual claim by one model as a function of message packaging; our study measures departure from and flagging of a planted objective conflict as a function of hierarchy visibility across two models and five domains. The relevance is confined to the V4 versus V5 channel contrast.

verified.title: The Self-Correction Illusion: Role Relabeling Gates Explicit Error Flagging in Large Language Models
verified.resolved_title: The Self-Correction Illusion: Role Relabeling Gates Explicit Error Flagging in Large Language Models
verified.authors: Kuan-Yen Chen; Fang-Yi Su; Shih-Yen Lin; Bao Li; Jung-Hsien Chiang
verified.verification_source: arXiv export API record for 2606.05976 (title, authors, dates, comments, abstract)
verified.abstract_gist: A training-free intervention keeps an erroneous claim byte-identical and varies only its message role (agent thought, user, tool response, or system memory) across 12 model-domain combinations. Relabeling from thought to an external role raises the explicit-correction rate by 23 to 93 percentage points in 10 of 12 settings, so the self-correction gap is largely an artifact of role labeling in the chat template, with the best label domain-dependent.
verified.use: Cite as the confound we must control: the message role that carries the parent brief, sibling mandates and ledger could itself gate the FLAGGED rate independent of content. Use it to justify reporting which role each visibility tier occupies and to motivate a role-held-constant check.
verified.differentiation: Chen et al. vary the role of an erroneous claim and measure whether the model flags the error; we vary how much organizational context a worker sees and measure whether it flags or departs from a conflicting instruction. Their result is a mechanism-level warning for our design, not a competing measurement of hierarchy visibility.

verified.title: Will the Agent Recuse, and Will It Stop? Measuring LLM-Agent Compliance with In-Band Governance Signals at the Access Door and Mid-Flight

verified.use: Cite in the Suite B design discussion for the finding that mid-task cooperative signals over a live channel are honored inconsistently and model-dependently, which sets expectations for how a peer-progress tool or live ledger update might or might not redirect a running worker; also for the harness-enforcement backstop argument.
verified.differentiation: Munirathinam measures whether agents obey explicit stop or deny signals from infrastructure; our signals are not commands but context about the hierarchy, and the outcome is whether the worker reconciles a conflict with the parent objective. Both concern live in-band information reaching a running agent, but ours has no directive semantics.

verified.abstract_gist: PrincipalBench is a 75-item multi-turn benchmark with leak probes, dual judges and an integrity-audit gate that measures whether an agent stays loyal to the principal who briefed it while conversing with a counterparty whose interests diverge. verified.use: Cite in the organization-theory layer as the principal-agent framing applied to LLM agents, and for the empirical leak versus over-refusal trade-off as an analogue to our adherence versus flagging tension.
verified.differentiation: PrincipalBench pits a principal against an adversarial counterparty in a separate channel; our setting has a single hierarchy with no adversary, and the conflict is between the worker's literal instruction and the parent's objective. Loyalty there is about not leaking; here it is about whether visibility of the hierarchy changes whether the worker departs or flags.

verified.use: Cite as the system-level counterpart to our per-worker measurements: organization raises effectiveness and misalignment together, and our visibility ladder probes one mechanism (what each worker is shown) that could drive that divergence.
verified.differentiation: Shen et al. compare whole organizations to single agents on utility and misalignment; we hold the organization fixed and vary a single worker's view of it, measuring conflict handling with deterministic checkers. verified.title: What's in Your Agent's Context? Context Privilege Escalation Attacks against AI Agent Harness

verified.use: Cite as the primary academic source for how harnesses assemble sub-agent context and which message roles receive it, supporting the per-harness policy table and the role-confound discussion; the 12-harness list is a cross-check for the table's coverage.
verified.differentiation: Li et al. study context assembly as an attack surface; we study it as an organizational visibility variable and measure benign conflict handling rather than exploitation. The descriptive layer (which sources land in which roles) is shared; the outcomes are unrelated.

verified.abstract_gist: The Roundtable Context Window Test varies coordination content (shared state, role instructions, prior discussion, tool outputs) while holding total budget, position order, task family and scoring fixed, and finds three commercial models degrade sharply only once residual task evidence falls to a few hundred tokens at W=4096. verified.use: Cite to support our length-matched control: RCWT shows coordination content per se does not degrade task performance when task evidence is intact, which strengthens the inference that our hierarchy effects come from content, not length.
verified.differentiation: RCWT measures recall accuracy under budget displacement; we measure conflict handling under semantically meaningful hierarchy context with length held fixed. RCWT's null for coordination volume is the premise our filler control tests in our own setting.

verified.use: Cite as the production precedent for treating a sub-agent raising a problem to its coordinator (our FLAGGED class) as a first-class protocol outcome rather than a failure, and for its taxonomy of sub-agent failure modes alongside MAST.

verified.differentiation: Acharya proposes middleware and evaluates workflow completion; we isolate the visibility variable experimentally and classify per-worker conflict handling with deterministic checkers. verified.use: Cite as the closest security-side study of the exact orchestrator-worker pattern under test: sub-agent outputs are consumed by the orchestrator as trusted summaries, which is the upward channel the visibility study leaves fixed while varying the downward one. The reasoning versus non-reasoning finding is a useful contrast with the study's null effect of the xhigh reasoning option.
verified.differentiation: Attacks the upward flow (sub-agent to orchestrator) for exfiltration; the visibility study manipulates the downward flow (what the orchestrator reveals to the worker) and measures objective adherence.

verified.abstract_gist: Tracks a cryptographic canary through EXPOSED, PERSISTED, RELAYED and EXECUTED stages across 950 runs, five frontier LLMs, six attack surfaces and five defense conditions, reframing injection as a pipeline-architecture problem. Every model is fully exposed but outcomes diverge downstream (Claude 0/164 at memory-write, GPT-4o-mini 53% propagation, DeepSeek 0% or 100% by surface), write-node placement is the highest-leverage decision, and all four defenses fail on at least one surface.
verified.use: Cite for the stage-level (not binary) outcome taxonomy, which parallels the ADHERED/FLAGGED/DEVIATED ladder, and for direct evidence that DeepSeek's relay behavior is surface-specific, relevant when interpreting DeepSeek V4 Flash's lower departure rate.
verified.differentiation: Adversarial canary propagation through pipeline stages; the visibility study tracks a benign objective conflict through a single worker and classifies its handling, with no persistence or execution stages.

The specific inter-agent-message, memory and installed-skill surfaces claimed by the candidate are not enumerated in the abstract and need a body check before being stated.
verified.differentiation: Single-agent defense against context-aware injection with a security-utility metric; no orchestration hierarchy, no benign conflicts, no adherence taxonomy.

verified.abstract_gist: Empirical study of how multi-agent design choices (agent roles, communication topology, memory/context visibility) trade off task performance against attack resistance across browser, desktop and code environments and 13 configurations, with stagewise evaluation from planning refusal to full attack completion. verified.use: Cite as the security-side counterpart to our visibility manipulation: they vary what context each agent can see (the memory axis) and find no universally safe architecture; we vary hierarchy visibility and find no silent deviation but rising announced departure. Also supports the paper's claim that harness defaults on cross-agent context are a design variable with measurable consequences.
verified.differentiation: They inject adversarial content and measure attack completion under varied memory/topology; we inject a benign objective conflict and measure whether the worker adheres, flags, or departs. Their independent variable overlaps ours (context visibility) but their dependent variable is attack success, not objective-directed departure.

verified.use: Cite in the harness policy section: the orchestrator ledger and sibling mandates we expose at V4/V5 are exactly the kind of 'agent context data' whose provenance a worker cannot verify; ADI shows that production harnesses do not separate trusted from untrusted context, which is the premise for treating parent-brief visibility as a trust decision.
verified.differentiation: Adversarial data disguised as trusted metadata, attacking real products; we expose genuine (non-adversarial) hierarchy context and measure objective-directed behavior. Complementary threat model, not overlapping measurement.

verified.use: Cite alongside instruction-hierarchy work when noting that model-level separation of instruction from data is the architectural alternative to harness-level labeling of parent brief versus worker instruction; our conditions test what happens when both are presented as instruction-bearing context with no such separation.

verified.differentiation: Misinformation-attack ranking over graph edges in peer topologies; no hierarchy of legitimate objectives, no adherence taxonomy, open models only.

verified.differentiation: Varies how the principal instructs and measures dishonesty toward a third party; this study holds the instruction fixed and varies visibility of the parent objective, measuring objective-directed departure and flagging rather than ethics.

verified.use: One-line support in the organization-theory section for the claim that raising a conflict (the FLAGGED class) has a human analogue in observers reporting rather than executing; useful mainly to complete the Köbis line of work.
verified.differentiation: Studies third-party observers of a delegation, not the delegate's own response to an instruction that conflicts with a higher objective; the analogy to FLAGGED is loose.

verified.title: Putting AI on the Org Chart: Evidence on Delegation and Oversight
verified.resolved_title: Putting AI on the Org Chart: Evidence on Delegation and Oversight
verified.authors: Emma Wiles, Megan Hsu, Julie Bedard, Matthew Kropp

verified.abstract_gist: A survey of 1,261 managers finds 23 percent work in organizations that have placed AI agents on org charts, and a randomized experiment gives managers identical error-laden drafts labeled as from an AI tool, an AI employee, or a human employee. Average effects on error catching are small, but among managers whose organizations already have AI employees the AI-employee label reduces monitoring intensity by 16 percent, increases reliance on others' review, and shifts perceived accountability toward the AI; managers monitor most when told the work came from a human employee.
verified.use: Management layer: the manager-side complement to this study's worker-side manipulation, showing that how an AI agent's organizational position is framed changes oversight, so hierarchy-visibility choices in harnesses are governance decisions on both sides of the delegation. Cite for the 16 percent monitoring reduction and the accountability shift.
verified.differentiation: Manipulates the principal's beliefs about the agent's role and measures human oversight; this study manipulates what the agent itself sees and measures the agent's behavior.

verified.abstract_gist: A real-effort natural field experiment in which workers hired for an identical job either are or are not told the organization's purpose, and the treatment raises unrequested extra work by roughly half.
