verified.title: The impact of AI transparency and AI authorization on human performance in AI-to-human delegation
verified.resolved_title: The impact of AI transparency and AI authorization on human performance in AI-to-human delegation
verified.authors: Jian Tang, Yunran Wang, Xinxue Zhou, Yuxiang Chris Zhao, Yiwei Jiang
verified.verification_source: Crossref API record for DOI 10.1007/s10660-026-10166-9 (title, authors, container-title, published 2026-07-07) plus Springer article page via WebFetch (abstract, publication date 07 July 2026)
verified.abstract_gist: Two between-subjects experiments grounded in principal-agent theory test how an AI principal's transparency (advantage vs. function vs. control information) and explicit authorization affect the performance of human agents it delegates to. Function information raises classification accuracy, advantage information raises volume, authorization helps, and epistemic uncertainty mediates the effect; the authors frame the design as addressing the hidden-action problem.
verified.use: Cite in the organization-theory layer as the mirror-image case: an experimental manipulation of how much a delegatee is told about its principal, showing that principal transparency (specifically information about what the principal does and why) changes agent performance through reduced epistemic uncertainty; supports framing the parent brief as a transparency variable rather than mere context length.
verified.differentiation: Roles are reversed (AI principal, human agents), the outcome is task accuracy and volume rather than adherence-versus-departure on a planted instruction-objective conflict, and there is no hierarchy of visibility tiers or announced/silent deviation coding. It supplies the theory (principal-agent, hidden action, epistemic uncertainty), not the measurement.

verified.title: Even More Deception: Objective Misalignment in Mixed-Motive LLM Multi-Agent Systems
verified.resolved_title: Even More Deception: Objective Misalignment in Mixed-Motive LLM Multi-Agent Systems
verified.authors: Marylou Fauchard, Florian Carichon, Margarida Carvalho, Golnoosh Farnadi
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2607.26120 (submitted 28 Jul 2026; comments: Accepted at AIWILD@ICLR 2026)
verified.abstract_gist: Evaluates objective misalignment in Werewolf by secretly modifying one agent's objective while preserving its role, across four model families and sizes, four roles and three objective formulations, with a dual analysis of private reasoning and public cheap talk. Compromised agents develop distinct objective-dependent reasoning that stays largely invisible in their public behavior, and misalignment degrades collective outcomes, worse under asymmetric information and specialized roles.
verified.use: Cite when motivating the announced-versus-silent deviation split and the decision to inspect reasoning tokens separately from the output: it documents the case where an objective change is visible in internal reasoning but not in public messages, the failure mode our checkers are designed to catch and which we did not observe.
verified.differentiation: The objective change is imposed adversarially and hidden by design in a mixed-motive game with no principal-agent hierarchy; our setting plants a conflict between a literal instruction and a cooperative parent objective and varies how much of the hierarchy the worker can see. They measure deception concealment; we measure departure and disclosure toward the parent's goal.

verified.title: Theory of Mind in Action: The Instruction Inference Task in Dynamic Human-Agent Collaboration
verified.resolved_title: Theory of Mind in Action: The Instruction Inference Task in Dynamic Human-Agent Collaboration
verified.authors: Fardin Saad, Pradeep K. Murukannaiah, Munindar P. Singh
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2507.02935 (submitted 26 Jun 2025, v3 revised 17 Apr 2026; 66 pages, code on GitHub; no journal ref)
verified.abstract_gist: Introduces the Instruction Inference task, in which an agent helps a principal reach a goal by interpreting incomplete or ambiguous instructions from shared context, and presents Tomcat, an LLM agent with few-shot chain-of-thought and commonsense-prompt variants on GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1 and Gemma-3-27B. Against 52 human participants given the same information, Fs-CoT Tomcat on GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 matches human intent accuracy, action optimality and planning optimality.
verified.use: Cite as the mechanism paper: intent inference from shared context is the capability that lets a worker recognize that the literal instruction conflicts with the principal's objective, which is the prerequisite for the flags and announced departures we observe once the parent brief is visible; also supports the observation that more capable models depart more.
verified.differentiation: Their instructions are incomplete or ambiguous and inference toward the principal's intent is the scored success criterion; ours are complete but deliberately in conflict with the objective, and the question is whether the worker adheres, flags or departs. They vary prompting strategy and model; we vary the visibility of the hierarchy while holding the instruction fixed.

verified.title: Can LLM Agents Sustain Long-Horizon Organizational Dynamics?
verified.resolved_title: Can LLM Agents Sustain Long-Horizon Organizational Dynamics?
verified.authors: Xuancheng Zhu, Yang Yue, Shuaibing Wan, Zihan Dou, Xiaohan Zhang, Yongrui Liu, Guoshun Nan
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2606.01199 (submitted 31 May 2026; no comments or journal ref)
verified.abstract_gist: Frames long-horizon organizational simulation as a memory-centered coordination problem and introduces TaskWeave, a hierarchical agentic framework with a Formulate-Partition-Diagnose-Align planning cycle and dependency-aware trace memory. In a year-long IT company simulation it is compared with other multi-agent frameworks on organizational coherence, execution grounding and enterprise NLP utility, and the authors argue structured simulation memory is key to reliable organizational simulators.
verified.use: Cite in the Suite B outlook as a hierarchy simulation in which goals propagate through explicit delegation tiers over a long horizon; a natural environment for testing whether visibility effects persist across many rounds and levels rather than a single delegation hop.
verified.differentiation: TaskWeave optimizes coherence and grounding of a whole simulated organization and does not plant instruction-objective conflicts, vary what a subordinate sees of its superiors' briefs, or code adherence, flagging and departure at the worker level. Note the abstract does not state the 15-agent, three-tier figures given in the candidate note; those need confirmation from the full text before being quoted.

verified.title: When Does Hierarchy Help? Benchmarking Agent Coordination in Event-Driven Industrial Scheduling
verified.resolved_title: When Does Hierarchy Help? Benchmarking Agent Coordination in Event-Driven Industrial Scheduling
verified.authors: Ziqi Wang, Yuhao Yang, Zhiwei Ling, Wenzhuo Qian, Hailiang Zhao
verified.verification_source: arXiv abs page 2605.13172 (submitted 13 May 2026; no comments or journal ref; the NLPCC 2026 acceptance mentioned in the candidate note is not on the arXiv record)
verified.abstract_gist: DESBench is a discrete-event industrial scheduling benchmark for agent coordination under multi-timescale decisions, partial observability and coupled constraints, scoring effectiveness, constraint alignment, coordination efficiency and robustness across centralized, hierarchical, heterarchical and holonic paradigms. Centralized coordination is robust but scales poorly, hierarchical decomposition is efficient but suffers cross-level misalignment, heterarchical is flexible but communication-heavy, and holonic satisfies constraints well but loses global robustness.
verified.use: Cite in the architectures section for the finding that hierarchical coordination produces cross-level misalignment: an outcome-level, benchmark-scale symptom of the same information-flow gap between tiers that our visibility manipulation isolates at the single-worker level; also supports the per-harness policy table's premise that what flows down the hierarchy is a design choice with measurable consequences.
verified.differentiation: DESBench varies the coordination topology and measures constraint alignment across many agents; it does not hold topology fixed and vary how much of the parent's brief one worker can read, nor does it plant a conflict or distinguish announced from silent departures. Its misalignment is emergent scheduling error, not instruction-versus-objective conflict resolution.

harness.harness: Claude Code agent teams (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS; lead + teammates; shared task list; mailbox; SendMessage)
harness.default_visibility: Parent conversation: NONE. A teammate is a full separate Claude Code session: 'Each teammate has its own context window. When spawned, a teammate loads the same project context as a regular session: CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, and skills. It also receives the spawn prompt from the lead. The lead's conversation history does not carry over.' Parent objective reaches the teammate only if the lead writes it into the spawn prompt (best-practice section: 'Include task-specific details in the spawn prompt'). Claude launches a teammate 'when it calls the Agent tool with a name while agent teams are enabled', so the spawn prompt is the Agent tool's `prompt` field. Teammates from a subagent definition get its body appended to the default system prompt (in-process) or in place of it (split pane); `skills` and (in-process) `mcpServers` fields are ignored and loaded from project/user settings instead. Messages arriving over SendMessage are labelled as coming 'from another Claude session, not from you', and a relayed approval claim is treated as untrusted. Requires an interactive session: with -p or the Agent SDK 'Claude doesn't spawn teammates, and a subagent that Claude names runs as an ordinary subagent'. Teammates inherit the lead's permission mode and effort level; plan-mode teammates work read-only until the lead session auto-approves their plan ('without the lead reviewing it').
harness.returned_to_parent: Final answer only, via an idle notification: 'when a teammate finishes and stops, it automatically notifies the lead and includes its final answer in the notification. A teammate whose turn ends on an API error notifies the lead that it failed and includes the error text.' Messages between agents are 'delivered automatically to recipients. The lead doesn't need to poll for updates.' Shutdown requests can be approved or rejected 'with an explanation'. harness.default_visibility: Parent conversation: NONE, and no fork option. Each agent() call spawns an ordinary subagent whose only task input is the prompt string the script composes: 'A dynamic workflow is a JavaScript script that orchestrates many subagents at once'; 'The workflow runtime executes the script in an isolated environment, separate from your conversation. Intermediate results stay in script variables instead of landing in Claude's context.' The bundled workflow-authoring reference (loaded this run, v2.1.248+) adds: 'Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data.' Whether the worker sees the parent objective, sibling results, or a ledger is entirely a property of the script text: prior agent() results are plain variables that the script may or may not interpolate into later prompts. agent() options: label, phase, schema (forces a StructuredOutput tool call), model, effort ('low'..'max'), isolation:'worktree', agentType (custom subagent type from the same registry as the Agent tool, whose system prompt then applies). Workers are subagents, so the sub-agents page's startup list applies (own system prompt, delegation prompt, CLAUDE.md hierarchy, git-status snapshot, preloaded skills); the prompt-caching section confirms same-prefix agents share 'the same tools-and-system-prompt prefix' keyed by model, effort, agent type, tools, output schema and working directory. harness.returned_to_parent: agent() 'resolves to' the subagent's final text as a string, or the schema-validated object; 'An agent() call resolves to null if you stop it mid-run or it hits an unrecoverable API error' (pipeline keeps the null; parallel never rejects). The script's own return value is the single thing that reaches the conversation: 'Claude's context holds only the final answer'; the SDK entry says the tool 'returns one consolidated result'. The runtime records every agent's result for resume (journal.jsonl in the run's transcript directory, per the authoring reference) and the human can drill into any agent in /workflows 'to read its prompt, recent tool calls, and result'. Claude receives the persisted script path when the run starts.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: None injected. The comparison table lists 'Where intermediate results live: Script variables' for workflows versus 'A shared task list' for agent teams and 'Claude's context window' for subagents. Siblings share only a prompt cache, not content: 'Agents in the same run can read each other's prompt cache', with all-but-first agents in a fan-out held up to CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS (5000 ms default). Cross-item context exists only when the script builds a barrier (parallel) and feeds results into later prompts, e.g. the adversarial-verify and judge-panel patterns in the authoring reference. Nested workflow() calls share the run's concurrency cap, agent counter and budget, one level deep.

harness.harness: Microsoft Copilot Studio multi-agent: child agents (inline) and connected agents (Copilot Studio, A2A, Foundry, Fabric, M365 Agents SDK) under the standard harness generative orchestration
harness.default_visibility: Two different defaults. CHILD AGENT: full parent context, not switchable: 'A child agent, by contrast, always receives the parent's context' (patterns page) and 'It runs inside the parent and always receives the parent's conversation context, with no setting to exclude it' (context-design page); 'By default, a child agent receives a natural language task to accomplish from the main agent when the agent calls it.' CONNECTED AGENT: the 'Pass conversation history to this agent' checkbox, 'enabled by default'; clearing it 'limits the information being passed to the agent to just the explicit task that the main agent wants the other agent to complete' so the agent 'works only from the inputs the parent sends, not the full conversation.' The context-design table gives the subagent's active context as 'Its initial request, plus parent-provided inputs and any included parent context, within its own orchestration layer context'; 'The orchestration layer also passes a longer conversation context to components such as knowledge and to subagents without explicit configuration.' Subagents are not told they are orchestrated: 'Subagents don't inherently know they're part of an orchestration. Without explicit guidance, they behave as standalone agents and send messages directly to the user.' Instruction precedence: 'The platform injects system-level instructions by using strong language (MUST, DO NOT, NEVER). Instructions written with soft language ... lose priority when they conflict.' Recommended reinforcement: put 'Return your findings only. Don't reply to the user.' in the delegated task text as well as in the subagent's instructions. Parent cannot stop a running subagent: 'Telling the parent agent, "You're the only agent that talks to the user," doesn't work.' The GitHub Copilot harness differs: the parent is the sole communicator and 'Connected agent messages pass through the parent's AI layer at every turn.'
harness.returned_to_parent: Child agent: 'When it completes its task, it returns a natural language summary of what happened during its execution' plus any maker-defined typed outputs. Generic contract: 'The parent can't see the subagent's exchange with the user and learns the result only through the defined outputs and implicit response'; 'Only two types of information return' (explicit outputs and implicit context); topic variables and multi-turn exchanges inside a subagent stay hidden unless returned. Connected agents have separate transcripts ('you have separate transcripts for it'), correlated by telemetry identifiers. Recommended output contract: answered (Boolean), scopedRequest, interactionSummary, findings, openQuestions. 'Citations might not always be maintained when passing outputs back.' After running options let the parent respond immediately using the child's outputs as context.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: Not stated for subagent-to-subagent visibility; nothing describes a child or connected agent seeing another's context or outputs. The orchestration layer holds 'component descriptions, input descriptions, output descriptions, plan state, implicit responses' and routes by description; multiple child agents can fire on the same activity in creation or Priority order. Guidance assumes non-overlapping knowledge per subagent because 'one subagent finds the answer first' and the other duplicates or skips. Connected-agent nesting is limited: an agent that has connected agents cannot itself be a connected agent of another main agent.
harness.knobs: Connected agent: 'Pass conversation history to this agent' (default on), local description override, 'Let other agents connect to and use this one' (agent Settings), must be published and in the same environment; Child agent: Inputs (required flag, Should prompt user, reprompts, Condition, Action if no entity found), Outputs (typed), After running: Don't respond (default) | Write the response with generative AI | Send specific response | Send an adaptive card; 'When will this be used?' triggers (message received, custom client event, activity, conversation changes, invoked, redirected to, user inactive, plan completes, AI-generated response about to be sent with ContinueResponse), Condition (Power Fx), Priority, Enabled toggle; per-tool 'Allow agent to decide dynamically when to use this tool'; scopedRequest input pattern; explicit redirect from a topic with input/output variables; choice of standard harness vs GitHub Copilot harness.
harness.static_instruction_confound: Platform-injected system-level instructions in MUST/NEVER language outrank soft maker instructions; each connected agent runs 'its own orchestration layer, its own instructions, and its own internal tool and knowledge calls' and may hold privileges the parent lacks; child and connected agents 'respect the Use general knowledge setting of the main agent'; the parent controls the connected agent's description locally and only the latest published version of a connected agent is used; the orchestration runtime can emit a system-generated explanation_of_tool_call message after a child responds when After running is Don't respond.

harness.harness: Kimi Code CLI sub-agents (Agent tool; AgentSwarm tool; built-in coder/explore/plan; custom agent files; experimental fork; tower mode)
harness.default_visibility: Parent conversation: NONE by default. 'A sub-agent receives a task description from the main Agent, works in its own isolated context, and then returns its conclusions. It does not communicate with the user directly'; 'Each sub-agent has a fully independent context window. It can only see the task description explicitly passed by the main Agent and cannot see the main Agent's conversation history.' The Agent tool's required inputs are 'prompt (complete task description) and description (a 3-5 word short summary)'; AgentSwarm launches subagents 'from a shared prompt_template and an items array' where '{{item}}' is substituted per subagent. Objective reaches the worker only if the main agent writes it into the prompt. Experimental full-transcript switch since 0.39.0 (2026-08-27): 'an optional fork parameter to subagent and swarm tools that starts the subagent with a snapshot of the calling agent's conversation history; set KIMI_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_SUBAGENT_FORK=1 or subagent_fork = true under [experimental]'. Custom agents delegated as sub-agents 'run without the built-in sub-agent framing ("your final message is the entire handoff")'. Each dispatch is shown to the user as an approval request with the task description unless an allow rule or Ask When Needed mode applies. Tower mode (experimental, 0.39.0+, KIMI_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_TOWER=1) is a separate multi-agent orchestration surface whose context policy is not documented on these pages.
harness.returned_to_parent: Final result only: 'The sub-agent's own intermediate reasoning and tool call records do not flow back; only the final result appears in the main Agent's context.' Background sub-agents deliver 'via a synthetic User message when done'; a sub-agent that finished while background tasks were running 'only reports completion after those tasks settle'. AgentSwarm 'waits for all subagents to finish, and returns an aggregated report'; a timed-out subagent 'is aborted and marked as failed in the aggregated report'. Full sub-agent history is persisted locally for the human, not the model: each sub-agent's 'wire.jsonl file that records prompts, message history, and final state'. Existing sub-agents can be resumed (resume / resume_agent_ids).
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: None. 'Multiple sub-agents can run in parallel without interfering with each other'; no inter-sub-agent messaging, shared task list, or ledger is documented for the Agent or AgentSwarm tools (the community thread kimi-cli discussion #969 records 'Subagents cannot communicate with each other'). The AgentSwarm aggregated report goes to the caller only. Recursion is bounded: 'The three built-in sub-agents cannot dispatch further sub-agents'; 'By default a custom agent inherits the built-in delegation allowlist (coder, explore, plan), whose members cannot dispatch further either, so delegation chains always terminate and unbounded recursive spawning is impossible without an explicit opt-in'; a custom agent opts in with an explicit `subagents` allowlist (`*` allows every type); changelog 0.35.0 (2026-08-12) 'Fix coder subagents spawning further subagents by default.'
harness.knobs: Agent tool: prompt, description, subagent_type (coder default | explore | plan | any discovered custom agent), resume, run_in_background, model (pool alias or 'primary'), fork (experimental); AgentSwarm: prompt_template with {{item}}, items (min 2), resume_agent_ids, subagent_type, model, fork; 'up to 128 total subagents'; ramp 5 immediately then 1 per 700 ms, KIMI_CODE_AGENT_SWARM_MAX_CONCURRENCY cap; must be the only tool call in its response; swarm mode toggle auto-approves AgentSwarm; timeouts [subagent] timeout_ms / KIMI_SUBAGENT_TIMEOUT_MS (2 h default, none in kimi -p) and [swarm] timeout_ms / KIMI_CODE_SWARM_TIMEOUT_MS; [secondary_model] subagent model pool (stable in 0.40.0), /secondary-model, force = true; custom agent frontmatter name, description, whenToUse, override, tools, disallowedTools, subagents; agent scopes Explicit (--agent-file) > Project (.kimi-code/agents/, .agents/agents/) > Extra (extra_agent_dirs) > User ($KIMI_CODE_HOME/agents/, ~/.agents/agents/) > Plugin > Built-in; --agent / --agent-file select the main agent; hooks at sub-agent completion; permission 'always allow' rules propagate to sub-agents; tower mode KIMI_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_TOWER=1.

harness.harness: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) subagent seam: spawn, fork, acp providers via dsh-tool-subagent; dsh-tool-subagent-control (send_message, interrupt_agent, list_agents)
harness.default_visibility: Provider-dependent, and the model-facing tool wording is derived from the provider's `inheritsParentContext` flag. spawn (in-process, default example in the tool README): 'The child starts with an empty conversation, so a task prompt must stand alone'; 'The fresh child receives the task content verbatim as its only user message in a new empty conversation, with the parent provider, model, reasoning effort, output-token limit, and working directory by default'; 'No parent conversation message is included'. Tool description the model sees under spawn/acp: 'The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation.' fork (in-process): 'seeds each child with the parent's completed conversation turns: the child sees every finished turn and none of the in-flight one'; the seed is 'a balanced completed-turn prefix of the parent's log — the parent's events up to and including its last turn/end'; 'The seed is captured once at start; later parent turns never reach the child'; the tool wording becomes 'it does not see the current in-flight turn'. acp (out-of-process, any ACP-compatible agent): 'the child gets its own runtime, session, model configuration, and tools'; 'the parent supplies only the task and the working directory'; 'ACP reads only its cwd'. Codex and Claude Code product providers also exist (dsh-subagent-codex, dsh-subagent-claude-code) and, like ACP, 'reject agentOptions before starting their transports'. The subsystem doc states the flag values outright: '`inheritsParentContext` describes only conversation seeding (`fork`: true; `spawn` and `acp`: false)'. Parent task: nothing beyond the delegation `prompt` (SubagentStartRequest.prompt = 'Content delivered as the child's user message'); no objective or brief field exists in the schema (`description` is a 3-5 word display label).
harness.knobs: (1) Provider choice per mounted tool instance (`provider: spawn | fork | acp | codex | claude-code | dsh-sdk`); several instances can coexist with distinct `toolName`s (the catalog shows `subagent` and `subagent_fork` side by side). (2) `maxDepth` (default 3; 0 forbids delegation; `'provider-managed'` for out-of-process providers); depth is durable in `SessionHeader.delegationDepth`, child = parent + 1, and cold resume cannot lower it. (3) `persona` (per-child system-prompt section that shadows `deployment:persona`), `toolFilter` (allow/deny global tools; they 'vanish from the child's prompt AND refuse to execute'), `agentOptions` (provider/model/reasoningEffort/maxTokens), `outputSchema` (structured result via a forced capture tool), each gated by a provider capability flag and rejected loudly when unsupported (ACP supports none). (4) `backgroundMode: one-shot | continuable` and `enableRunInBackground`; continuable children are durable sessions the parent can message. (5) `modelSelectionSettings` exposes `provider`/`model`/`reasoning_effort` fields plus `list_subagent_models`. (6) ACP provider: `command`, `args`, `cwd`, `permission: reject | allow`, credential-scrubbed `env`. No knob passes the parent's objective or a brief separately from the prompt; the only transcript knob is the provider switch to fork.
harness.returned_to_parent: Final output only. Tool description: 'The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps.' One-shot `SubagentResult` carries `output` (final assistant text), optional `structured` (when `outputSchema` was satisfied), `stopReason` (completed | max-tokens | refusal | aborted | error) and an optional sanitized `diagnostic` capped at 4096 UTF-8 bytes from which providers 'remove tool inputs, file contents, environment values, credentials, and raw protocol payloads'; a non-completed stop reason maps to an `isError` tool result rather than partial success. ACP: 'The parent receives only the child's final answer or a safe error — no intermediate messages or tool traffic crosses the boundary.' Background one-shot returns 'started background subagent job <id>' collected via `job_output`; continuable returns 'started subagent <childId>' and one settlement notice when the child's Activation ends. Observers (not the parent model) get paired `subagent/start` / `subagent/end` events and can enumerate children via `listChildren` / `listDescendants` without loading an agent.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: No shared ledger. `send_message` is strictly adjacent: 'permits only a direct parent or direct continuable child'; 'Siblings, ancestors beyond one edge, self-targets, stale Agent objects, and one-shot children are rejected.' Delivered messages are framed 'Agent <sender-id> sent a message:' and 'provenance records the sender but grants no authority'. `list_agents` (separately loadable `/list-agents` plugin) shows the caller's continuable children with status running/idle/ready, not siblings. In-process children 'get a new flat scope rather than inheriting parent registrations'; one-shot children share the parent's working directory (ACP shares only cwd).
harness.static_instruction_confound: The in-process child shares the process's global system-prompt composition: 'A configured persona shadows global prompt text in the child's scope' and the tool injects `ctx.systemPrompt`, so whatever the deployment's persona/prompt plugins contribute reaches a spawn or fork child unless a per-child `persona` shadows it. The fetched docs do not mention AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md-style project files at all, so any repository-file confound is not stated. ACP and other out-of-process children get the child runtime's own prompt; a DSH child launched over ACP must use an isolated `DSH_HOME` so it cannot discover 'the launching person's profiles or credentials'.

harness.harness: Hermes Agent (Nous Research) delegate_task subagents (leaf / orchestrator roles, batch mode, worktree isolation, /review reviewer)
harness.default_visibility: Parent conversation: NONE. 'Subagents start with a completely fresh conversation. They have zero knowledge of the parent's conversation history, prior tool calls, or anything discussed before delegation. The subagent's only context comes from the goal and context fields the parent agent populates when it calls delegate_task.' Parent task: only what the parent writes into `goal` (required task description) and `context` (required, 'Full context the subagent needs'); the page's BAD/GOOD example shows `goal="Fix the error"` failing because the child cannot resolve 'the error'. 'The subagent receives a focused system prompt built from your goal and context, instructing it to complete the task and provide a structured summary of what it did, what it found, any files modified, and any issues encountered.' Exception to isolation: the repo context files (see static_instruction_confound). The separate `/review` reviewer 'inherits the primary agent's working context: any skills the primary agent had loaded ... are named in its briefing with an instruction to load them'. Each child has 'their own terminal sessions'; by default children share the parent's working directory.
harness.knobs: Per call: `goal`, `context`, `max_iterations` (default 50), `role: leaf | orchestrator` (leaf is default and cannot delegate), `background`, and batch `tasks=[{goal, context}, ...]`. Config `delegation.*`: `max_concurrent_children` (default 3, floor 1, no ceiling; also DELEGATION_MAX_CONCURRENT_CHILDREN), `max_spawn_depth` (default 1 = flat; 'Raise to 2 to allow orchestrator children to spawn leaf grandchildren; 3+ for deeper trees. There is no upper ceiling'), `orchestrator_enabled` (false forces all children to leaf), `worktree_isolation` (default false; each child gets `<repo>/.worktrees/subagent-<id>` on branch `hermes-subagent/subagent-<id>`, 'inspired by Muse Code's --subagent-worktree-isolation'), `model`/`provider`/`api_mode` overrides (empty model = inherit the parent's). `delegate_task does not accept a model-facing toolsets parameter. Each subagent inherits the parent's enabled toolsets so the model cannot grant a child capabilities that the parent does not have.' Blocked in children: `delegate_task` (leaf), `clarify`, `memory`, `send_message`, `cronjob`. Control actions `list`, `steer` (queue a course correction into a running child), `stop`. No knob passes the parent transcript or objective; the parent must author `context`.
harness.returned_to_parent: 'only its final summary enters the parent's context'. The child is instructed to return a structured summary (what it did, what it found, files modified, issues). The tool result carries `status` (`failed` plus a single most-informative error line on failure), timeout metadata (`timeout_seconds`, `timed_out_after_seconds`, `timeout_phase`), a `worktree` block when isolation is on (path, branch, commits, dirty status), and `live_transcripts` paths. Top-level calls run in the background: 'Hermes returns a handle immediately so the conversation can continue, then posts the result back as a new message'; batch results are 'sorted by task index to match input order regardless of completion order'; a stopped child's 'partial result still re-enters the conversation as a normal completion message'. Full child transcripts are written to `<hermes_home>/cache/delegation/live/<delegation_id>/task-<n>.log` (assistant text, thinking, tool calls) for a human or the parent to `tail -f`, i.e. an on-disk ledger the parent could read with a file tool but is not fed by default.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: No sibling messaging: `send_message` is blocked for children ('no cross-platform side effects'). Batch siblings run in a ThreadPoolExecutor and share the working directory unless `worktree_isolation` is on ('children can't clobber each other's edits'). The parent's `list` control returns its live children (subagent_id, goal, status, running_seconds, accepting_steer, live transcript path); children have no such view of each other. The live-transcript log files are the only ledger-like artifact and are readable from the filesystem, including remote terminal backends (Docker/Modal/SSH).
harness.static_instruction_confound: Explicitly documented: 'when the parent has a resolved workspace directory, every subagent's system prompt embeds that workspace's project context files (.hermes.md > AGENTS.md chain > CLAUDE.md > .cursorrules — the same discovery, priority, and size caps as the main agent's system prompt; SOUL.md is excluded).' Children also inherit the parent's API key, provider configuration and credential pool. Skills reach the /review reviewer by name only.
harness.evidence_quote: Subagents start with a completely fresh conversation.

harness.harness: OpenRouter `openrouter:subagent` server tool (Responses API and Chat Completions; worker model, nested server tools, experimental client-function inheritance)
harness.default_visibility: Parent conversation: NONE. Docs: 'Each task is independent: the worker sees only the task description (not the parent conversation) and keeps no memory between tasks.' Blog: 'The worker model sees only what the delegating model explicitly passes in the task_description. No parent conversation, no prior context, no memory between tasks. Each delegation is a clean, isolated unit of work.' Parent task: only what the orchestrating model writes into `task_description` ('Everything the worker needs to complete the task: full context, inputs, constraints, and the expected output format. The worker sees only this description.'), plus a static developer-set `instructions` system prompt for the worker. The worker model defaults to the outer request's model unless `parameters.model` is set.
harness.knobs: `parameters.model` (any OpenRouter model; default = outer request model), `instructions` (worker system prompt), `tools` (only OpenRouter server tools such as `openrouter:web_search` / `openrouter:web_fetch`; client function tools in the nested array are rejected with a 400; 'The subagent may not list itself'), `max_tool_calls` (1-25), `max_completion_tokens`, `reasoning` (effort, max_tokens), `temperature`. Experimental, Responses API only: `inherit_functions: true` gives the worker every top-level client function tool, or `inherited_function_names` copies named ones, with a suspension/replay contract in which the worker's function calls surface to the client and the worker is resumed with the client's results. Model-side call arguments: `task_name`, `task_description`. Caps: 'Recursion is blocked. The subagent can't call itself. A depth header and self-reference check prevent unbounded nesting, and delegations are capped at 10 per request' (blog); docs: 'Each inner subagent call carries an x-openrouter-subagent-depth header; the subagent tool is stripped from any sub-call, so a worker can never re-enter the subagent. Task executions are also capped per request'. No knob shares any parent context; there is no objective or brief field.
harness.returned_to_parent: Final text only. 'On success the tool result contains the outcome text, the task name, and the model that produced it': `{status: "ok", model, task_name, outcome}`; on failure `{status: "error", task_name, error}` and 'the calling model continues without the outcome'. 'The worker's tool use happens inside the tool call; only its final text is returned to your model.' A completed `openrouter:subagent` output item (new id, same `call_id`) carries `task_name`, `task_description`, `model`, `outcome`; the `response.output_item.added` event for a suspended item is deferred until the spawning call's arguments finish streaming.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: None. Multiple delegations in one request are independent tasks with 'no memory between tasks'; no messaging, no shared state, no ledger. Blog: 'Each delegation is a clean, isolated unit of work.'
harness.static_instruction_confound: Only the developer-set `instructions` string reaches the worker as a system prompt; no repository files or platform instructions are read. If `inherit_functions` / `inherited_function_names` is set, the worker also sees the copied top-level function tool definitions (names, descriptions, schemas), which is the only channel through which parent-request content other than `task_description` reaches it.
harness.evidence_quote: the worker sees only the task description (not the parent conversation)
harness.doc_version_or_date: Docs page undated; announcement blog 'Kenny Rogers · 6/16/2026' (https://openrouter.ai/blog/announcements/subagent-server-tool/). Fetched 2026-09-03.

harness.harness: Anthropic multi-agent evaluation harnesses in the Claude Opus 5 System Card §8.11.3 (N-agent team; async subagents) for BrowseComp and ProgramBench
harness.default_visibility: Two harnesses with opposite policies. Async subagents (the hierarchical one): 'a lead agent which can spawn asynchronous, long-lived subagents while retaining direct access to the task tools. The spawning tool returns immediately with a confirmation rather than waiting on subagent execution. Each subagent sees only the instructions provided by the lead, not the original task description, and subagents can message any other agent and the lead.' N-agent team (peers, N=5 or 10): 'One agent is designated the lead and is responsible for coordination and submitting the final answer if needed, but all agents have identical tools and all see the full task description.' Both: 'Every agent has a 1M token limit'; common tools are web search, web fetch, programmatic tool calling (code execution and bash) for search tasks, and bash for coding; on ProgramBench 'each agent works in its own checkout of the task repository and can share code with other agents via Git'. The card does not state whether subagents receive any system prompt beyond the lead's instructions.
harness.knobs: Research harness, not a product: choice of harness (team vs async subagents), N (5 or 10), and no cap on subagent count ('There is no cap on the number of subagents that can be spawned'). Lead-only tools in the async harness: create subagent, delete subagent (frees concurrency slots), check subagent status (working, idle, or terminated). Everyone has Send Message and Wait for Message. Results were gathered 'on a pre-release configuration of Claude Opus 5, with an unreleased effort configuration and without safeguards classifiers'.
harness.returned_to_parent: 'A subagent's final response is delivered to the lead as a message, after which the subagent idles until the lead wakes it with new instructions.' Messages are 'inserted following the recipient's next tool result'. 'For search tasks, only the lead agent's final submission is graded.' Nothing about subagent transcripts reaching the lead; BrowseComp runs were 'scanned after the fact with a verifier Claude and an automated pipeline to identify answer leakage'.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: Full peer messaging in both harnesses: Send Message 'delivers a message to one or more teammates' and Wait for Message 'blocks sampling until an incoming message arrives'; in the async harness 'subagents can message any other agent and the lead'. No shared ledger beyond Git on ProgramBench (per-agent checkouts, code shared via Git). The lead sees subagent status (working/idle/terminated) but no transcript.
harness.static_instruction_confound: Not stated. The card describes only task tools, messaging tools and the lead's instructions; no repository or platform instruction files are mentioned for the BrowseComp harness, and for ProgramBench each agent has its own repository checkout (so any in-repo instruction files would be visible to every agent, but the card does not say whether they are loaded).
harness.evidence_quote: Each subagent sees only the instructions provided by the lead, not the original task description
harness.doc_version_or_date: System Card dated July 24, 2026; changelog August 19, 2026 (changes listed do not touch §8.11). Section 8.11.3 'Multi-Agent Harnesses', pp. 171-172 of the PDF. Fetched 2026-09-03.

harness.harness: Anthropic Managed Agents multiagent orchestration (coordinator roster, session threads, agent_toolset_20260401) plus the session-log / getEvents() primitive from the engineering post
harness.default_visibility: Docs page (unchanged from the existing row): 'each agent runs in its own session thread, a context-isolated event stream with its own conversation history'; 'Tools, MCP servers, and context are not shared'; shared sandbox, filesystem and vault credentials. The delegated task 'arrives on the child's own stream as an agent.thread_message_received event' with `content`; that message is the child's only view of the parent task. Engineering post (Apr 08, 2026) adds the architecture behind it: the session is 'a context object that lives outside Claude's context window ... context is durably stored in the session log. The interface, getEvents(), allows the brain to interrogate context by selecting positional slices of the event stream ... pick up from wherever it last stopped reading, rewinding a few events before a specific moment to see the lead up, or rereading context before a specific action.' The post frames getEvents() as the brain's window onto its own session log (the harness uses it to rebuild context after a crash or compaction); it does not say a child thread can call getEvents() on the coordinator's primary thread, and the docs page exposes no agent-facing tool for reading another thread's events. Per-thread event streams (`/v1/sessions/{session_id}/threads/{thread_id}/stream`, same `event_deltas[]` parameter) are a client API, and 'a child thread's previews never appear on the session-level stream'.
harness.knobs: As in the existing row: `multiagent: {type: 'coordinator', agents: [...]}` with `{type:'agent', id, version?}`, `{type:'self'}`, `{type:'advisor', model}`; `tools: [{type:'agent_toolset_20260401'}]` giving `list_agents` / `send_to_agent`; per-agent MCP servers and session-scoped `vault_ids`; session budget shared across threads; `user.interrupt` per thread; max 20 unique roster agents, 25 concurrent threads, one delegation level only. New from this pass: client-side per-thread streaming with `event_deltas[]` to 'preview a subagent's text as the model generates it'; `getEvents()` positional slicing described in the engineering post as the harness-internal context interface (no public parameter documented for it). Still no knob shares the coordinator's transcript with a child.
harness.returned_to_parent: Unchanged: reports or questions as messages ('On the primary thread, an agent sent a report or question to the coordinator. Includes from_session_thread_id, from_agent_name, and content'). The primary thread is 'a condensed view of all activity across all threads. You don't see the full activity from subagents, but you do see the start and end of their work, and blocking events such as tool permission requests.' 'Critical events are proxied to the primary thread'; the full child transcript is reachable only by the client via the thread's own event stream ('to watch a subagent live, open its own thread stream'). Engineering post: the session log 'sits outside the harness', so the durable record of every thread exists server-side regardless of what the coordinator's model sees.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: Unchanged: coordinator has `list_agents` and `send_to_agent`; nothing documents roster agents seeing or messaging each other; the advisor is reachable only from the primary thread ('Roster agents cannot'). The session log is a ledger held by the platform, exposed to clients per thread, not to sibling agents. Shared filesystem remains the only implicit cross-agent channel.
harness.static_instruction_confound: Each roster agent runs under its own agent definition (model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers, skills); session-level agent configuration overrides apply to the coordinator and its `self` copies only. Shared sandbox and filesystem mean any instruction files on disk are readable by every thread with file tools, but the docs do not describe automatic loading of repository instruction files.
harness.evidence_quote: each agent runs in its own session thread, a context-isolated event stream
harness.doc_version_or_date: Docs page undated; beta header managed-agents-2026-04-01 (memory store: agent-memory-2026-07-22). Engineering post 'Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands', Published Apr 08, 2026 (https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents). Fetched 2026-09-03.

Added: the engineering post's getEvents() positional-slice interface as the session-log primitive (harness-internal, no agent-facing cross-thread read documented), the per-thread stream endpoint with event_deltas[] previews, and the explicit statement that the delegated task arrives on the child's stream as agent.thread_message_received.

harness.harness: Claude Code auto mode classifier at subagent handoffs (addition to the existing Claude Code sub-agents row)
harness.default_visibility: Not a visibility change for the worker; the post confirms the existing row's V0 framing from the safety side: 'Inside the subagent, the orchestrator's instruction is the user message, so tasks look fully authorized.' What the classifier itself sees: 'The classifier sees only user messages and the agent's tool calls; we strip out Claude's own messages and tool outputs, making it reasoning-blind by design'; it is a two-stage transcript classifier ('Stage 1 is a fast single-token (yes/no) filter instructed to err toward blocking; if it flags, stage 2 re-evaluates the same input with chain-of-thought reasoning'). Tiering: 'The transcript classifier sees everything else, including shell commands, web fetches, external tool integrations, subagent spawns, filesystem operations outside the project directory.' At delegation: 'The classifier runs at both ends of a subagent handoff: when work is delegated out and when results come back. The outbound check exists because, without it, the transcript classifier that monitors the subagent may not have the full context to know if the task it was given was originally intended by the user ... We catch it at delegation, while it's still recognizable as an agent choice rather than a user request.'
harness.knobs: Auto mode itself (the post positions it as replacing --dangerously-skip-permissions); deny-and-continue semantics when the classifier blocks. The post documents no per-subagent switch and does not say whether subagents inherit auto mode. The handoff checks are not configurable on the page.
harness.returned_to_parent: On return the classifier, not the parent model, reads the whole subagent transcript: 'The return check exists because a subagent that was benign at delegation could be compromised mid-run by a prompt injection in content it reads. Before results go back to the orchestrator, the classifier reviews the subagent's full action history. If it flags, we prepend a security warning for the agent that started the subagent rather than discard the results.' So the parent receives the subagent's result plus, when flagged, a prepended warning; the subagent's action history stays with the classifier.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: Not addressed. The classifier is a per-handoff observer over one subagent's action history; nothing about sibling or ledger visibility.
harness.static_instruction_confound: Not addressed on this page. The relevant confound is on the observer side: the classifier judges the outbound delegation against user messages only, and inside the subagent the delegation prompt occupies the user-message slot, which is exactly why the outbound check exists.
harness.evidence_quote: Inside the subagent, the orchestrator's instruction is the user message
harness.doc_version_or_date: Engineering post 'How we built Claude Code auto mode: a safer way to skip permissions', Published Mar 25, 2026. Fetched 2026-09-03.
harness.changed_since_first_table: Addition to the existing Claude Code sub-agents row (which currently has no mention of auto mode): the classifier runs at both ends of a handoff, reviews the subagent's full action history before results return, and prepends a security warning rather than discarding results; the page also independently confirms that the delegation prompt is the subagent's user message.

harness.harness: AWS Bedrock Agents (Classic) multi-agent collaboration: supervisor vs supervisor with routing; collaborator conversation-history relay
harness.default_visibility: Parent conversation: NONE by default. The collaborator receives only the request the supervisor routes to it plus its developer-written collaborationInstruction; history relay is an opt-in per-collaborator toggle: '(Optional) Turn on Enable conversation history if you want the supervisor agent to share context from previous conversations with this collaborator agent. If this is turned on, the supervisor will include the full history of the current session, including the user input text and the supervisor agent response from each turn of the conversation.' Parent task: in Supervisor mode the supervisor 'automatically creates and executes a plan across a set of collaborator agents and routes relevant requests and tasks to the appropriate collaborator agent' (the collaborator sees the routed sub-request, not the plan); in Supervisor with routing the user request itself is routed: 'If you want supervisor agent to route information to the appropriate collaborator agent to send the final response, select Supervisor with routing' and 'Assigning the supervisor agent the task of routing information reduces the latency.' Two modes on the console page: 'If you want supervisor agent to coordinate responses from the collaborator agents, select Supervisor.' Banner on every page: 'Amazon Bedrock Agents (now Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic) is no longer open to new customers.'
harness.returned_to_parent: Collaborator response returns to the supervisor, which 'coordinate[s] responses from the collaborator agents' into a final answer (Supervisor mode); in Supervisor with routing the chosen collaborator 'send[s] the final response' directly. Nothing on the pages says the collaborator's tool trace or reasoning returns; only the response.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: Not stated for collaborators. The supervisor knows collaborators through their collaborationInstruction text (the alternate collaboratorName 'will appear only in collaboration instructions'). With relayConversationHistory=TO_COLLABORATOR the collaborator receives every prior turn's user input and supervisor response, which can embed sibling results indirectly. Max 10 collaborators per supervisor.
harness.knobs: CreateAgent/UpdateAgent agentCollaboration: SUPERVISOR | SUPERVISOR_ROUTER | DISABLED. AssociateAgentCollaborator relayConversationHistory: TO_COLLABORATOR | DISABLED ('Set to TO_COLLABORATOR to specify that the supervisor agent will share context from previous conversations with this collaborator agent'); collaborationInstruction (required, 1 to 4000 chars); collaboratorName; console toggle 'Enable conversation history'.
harness.static_instruction_confound: Every collaborator is a full Bedrock Agent with its own agent instructions, action groups, knowledge bases and guardrails ('has all the capabilities of Amazon Bedrock Agents'); the collaborationInstruction is authored by the developer, not the supervisor model. harness.harness: Agno Teams (TeamMode coordinate / route / broadcast / tasks; share_member_interactions, add_team_history_to_members, determine_input_for_members, respond_directly)
harness.default_visibility: Parent conversation: NONE by default. Default flow (coordinate): 'Leader analyzes the input and decides which members to delegate to', 'Leader formulates a task for each selected member', 'Members execute and return results', 'Leader synthesizes results into a final response'. The member sees the leader-written task; the leader's system prompt instructs it to 'Write task descriptions that are self-contained: state the goal, provide relevant context from the conversation, and describe what a good result looks like.' History: 'Unlike team-level history, each member only has access to its own conversation history, not the history of other members or the team.' share_member_interactions default False: 'If True, send all previous member interactions to members.' add_team_history_to_members: 'member agents see the full team conversation rather than only their own interactions' (last num_team_history_runs team-level inputs and responses 'automatically to every message sent to the team members'). Route mode: 'The leader selects which member handles the request and returns the member's response directly. By default the leader can still craft the task; set determine_input_for_members=False to pass the user input through unchanged.' Broadcast: 'The leader delegates the same task to all members.' Tasks: 'Leader builds and executes a shared task list until the goal is complete.' A 'collaborate' mode no longer exists in current docs; 'mode overrides legacy flags'.
harness.returned_to_parent: Member result returns to the leader, which synthesizes (coordinate/broadcast/tasks) or returns it unchanged (route, or respond_directly=True: 'the team leader won't process responses from members and instead will return them directly'). show_members_responses controls display to the user, not model visibility.

harness.harness: PydanticAI agent delegation (delegate agent called inside a tool with deps and usage) and programmatic hand-off (message_history)
harness.default_visibility: Parent conversation: NONE by default. 'Agent delegation refers to the scenario where an agent delegates work to another agent, then takes back control when the delegate agent (the agent called from within a tool) finishes.' The delegate receives only the prompt the tool passes to run(), deps ('Pass the dependencies to the delegate agent's run method within the tool call'; 'Generally the delegate agent needs to either have the same dependencies as the calling agent, or dependencies which are a subset') and usage ('pass ctx.usage to the usage keyword argument of the delegate agent run so usage within that run counts towards the total usage of the parent agent run'). Transcript sharing is a code-level choice: 'To give another agent the previous conversation as context, pass message_history to its run method.' When shared: 'previous ModelRequest messages still contain the instructions used by the originating agent, but those instructions are not sent to the model again. The receiving agent uses its own instructions'; 'If message_history is set and not empty, a new system prompt is not generated.'
harness.returned_to_parent: Whatever the tool returns (example: 'we can simply return r.output from the tool'); usage accumulates into result.usage when ctx.usage is passed. 'a delegate agent cancelling itself surfaces to the parent as a failed tool return rather than cancelling the parent'. Temporal caveat: 'A tool running in a Temporal activity receives a copy of the run context, so usage=ctx.usage does not carry the delegate's usage back to the parent run.'
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: None built in; the shared deps object is the only channel and is developer-defined.

harness.harness: LlamaIndex AgentWorkflow handoffs (FunctionAgent/ReActAgent, can_handoff_to, root_agent, initial_state, Context state) and orchestrator pattern (sub-agents as tools)
harness.default_visibility: AgentWorkflow handoff: the handed-off agent sees the full shared chat history plus shared state. Source (multi_agent_workflow.py): one ChatMemoryBuffer is stored once in ctx.store['memory'] and every agent step reads 'input_messages = await memory.aget()', so prior agents' turns and tool results are all in the next agent's input; the handoff tool result injected into that history is 'Agent {to_agent} is now handling the request due to the following reason: {reason}.\nPlease continue with the current request.'; state is injected via 'Current state: {state} Current message: {msg}'. Orchestrator pattern: sub-agents are tools and receive only the wrapper's user_msg (example: 'Write some notes about the following: {prompt}') plus whatever state the wrapper copies in; 'tools always return back to the orchestrator'.
harness.returned_to_parent: Handoff: no return; control transfers and the workflow ends when 'an agent returns a final answer' ('At any point, the current active agent can choose to return control back to the user'). Orchestrator: the tool wrapper returns str(result) and usually writes to ctx.store state.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: Handoff: full shared memory and the state dict (e.g. research_notes, report_content, review) are visible to every agent. Orchestrator: sub-agents see only what the wrapper passes; the orchestrator sees tool returns.

harness.harness: CrewAI hierarchical process and per-task context (manager_llm / manager_agent, allow_delegation, Task.context, Crew(planning=True), knowledge_sources)
harness.default_visibility: Parent conversation: NONE by documented mechanism. A delegated coworker receives only what the delegating agent writes into the tool call 'Delegate work to coworker(task: str, context: str, coworker: str)' or 'Ask question to coworker(question: str, context: str, coworker: str)' (collaboration page). No official docs page states what the coworker sees beyond those arguments; the hierarchical-process page still contains no sentence about worker context (its only context sentence is 'Prioritize important context by enabling respect of the context window, which is now the default behavior'). The official source (lib/crewai/src/crewai/tools/agent_tools/base_agent_tools.py, main branch, fetched this run) closes the gap: the tool builds `Task(description=task, agent=selected_agent, expected_output=I18N_DEFAULT.slice('manager_request'))` and calls `selected_agent.execute_task(task_with_assigned_agent, context)`, so the worker's prompt is the manager-written task string plus the manager-written context string, nothing from the manager's own transcript. Delegation default: agents page 'Allow the agent to delegate tasks to other agents. Default is False.'; hierarchical-process page feature list: 'Delegation Control: Delegation is now disabled by default to give users explicit control.' Manager: 'A manager agent allocates tasks among crew members based on their roles and capabilities'; 'The manager assigns tasks strategically, considering each agent's capabilities and available tools.' Sequential chaining (tasks page): 'the output of one task is automatically relayed into the next one, but you can specifically define what tasks' output ... should be used as context for another task' via Task(context=[...]); 'forward references are rejected so sequential context stays explicit' (JSON crews). Crew(planning=True) (crews page): 'When activated before each Crew iteration, all Crew data is sent to an AgentPlanner that will plan the tasks and this plan will be added to each task description'; planning page: 'all Crew information is sent to an AgentPlanner that will plan the tasks step by step, and this plan will be added to each task description', default planner LLM gpt-4o-mini (requires an OpenAI key), sample plan lists every task, its agent, goal, expected output and step-by-step plan, so each crew task carries a crew-wide objective dose (V1/V2-like for the agent that executes that crew task; per the source above the ad hoc sub-Task built by the delegation tool does not carry it). knowledge_sources (crews page): 'Knowledge sources available at the crew level, accessible to all the agents'; knowledge page: 'Crew level knowledge sources will be used by all agents in the crew. Agent level knowledge sources will be used by the specific agent that is preloaded with the knowledge'; 'specialist gets: crew_knowledge + specialist_knowledge; generalist gets: crew_knowledge only'; knowledge is preloaded rather than tool-retrieved ('agents preloaded with knowledge will not need a retrieval persona or task').
harness.returned_to_parent: The coworker's answer returns as the string result of the delegation or question tool (source: `return selected_agent.execute_task(task_with_assigned_agent, context)`; errors return an i18n error string). Crew task results return as TaskOutput and feed later tasks through Task(context=[...]) or implicit previous-output chaining. The manager 'evaluates outcomes to ensure they meet the required standards' (Result Validation). No transcript sharing is documented anywhere.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: Sibling identities are visible only through the delegation and question tools when allow_delegation=True (the tool lists coworker roles on a lookup miss: 'agent_tool_unexisting_coworker' error enumerates roles). Sibling outputs reach a worker only when the developer lists them in Task(context=[...]) or the manager pastes them into the tool's `context` string. No shared transcript or ledger; crew `memory` ('short-term, long-term, entity memory') and crew-level knowledge_sources are the only shared stores; collaboration page: 'With memory enabled, agents learn from previous collaborations'.
harness.knobs: Agent(allow_delegation=True) (default False) exposes the two coworker tools whose `context` string is the manager-written dose; Crew(process=Process.hierarchical, manager_llm=...) ('Required when using a hierarchical process') or manager_agent=... (custom-manager-agent page: manager with allow_delegation=True, specialists allow_delegation=False to stop delegation loops); Task(context=[task_a, task_b]) selects which prior outputs are supplied; Crew(planning=True, planning_llm=...) injects the AgentPlanner plan into every crew task description; Crew(knowledge_sources=[...]) crew-wide vs Agent(knowledge_sources=[...]) per-agent; Crew(memory=True); Agent.system_template / prompt_template / response_template, use_system_prompt (default True), inject_date (default False), respect_context_window (default True, 'Keep messages under context window size by summarizing'); JSON crew and agent files (agents/<name>.jsonc) support the same fields.

harness.harness: eve (eve.dev) subagents: root-only built-in `agent` tool (copies of the root agent), declared subagents under agent/subagents/<id>/, extension-contributed subagents, remote agents
harness.default_visibility: Parent conversation: none, for every kind of child. Tool input schema comment: 'message: string; // all context the child needs; it never sees the parent's history'; 'The parent packs message with everything the child needs, since the child never sees the parent's history'; remote-agents page: 'The message must carry the full task, including any context the remote agent needs, because it never receives the parent's conversation history.' Root copy: 'The copy uses the root's instructions, connections, auth, and sandbox. It receives the same tools except for the root-only agent and Workflow, and starts with fresh conversation history and fresh state. Its file writes are immediately visible to the root.' Declared subagent: 'A declared subagent inherits nothing from the root's authored slots' (own instructions, tools, connections, skills, sandbox, hooks, extensions, nested subagents; state 'Fresh' for both kinds; 'defineState is never shared, for either kind'). The parent task reaches the child only through `message`. Who may call `agent`: 'agent is intentionally root-only. Copies created by it cannot call agent, and declared subagents never receive the built-in tool. If a stale or forced recursive call reaches execution, eve rejects it'; 'Child sessions can still call their own declared or remote subagents, but they receive neither Workflow nor the built-in agent.' Depth: 'eve does not apply a separate depth limit; nesting ends where the authored directory tree ends ... so limits.maxSubagentDepth no longer exists.' Session-context page: a child's ctx.session exposes `parent` ('the parent call, session, root session, and turn for a child subagent session'), i.e. lineage identifiers, not parent history; 'A subagent sees its own sandbox, not its parent's' (declared kind).
harness.returned_to_parent: Asynchronous only: 'The built-in agent always runs in the background ... each call returns { status: "working", taskId, agentId }, then task notifications wake the parent with updates or the final result'; declared and remote subagents: 'the call returns { status: "working", taskId, agentId } immediately, then task notifications wake the parent with updates, completion, failure, or cancellation. Human input requests surface separately on the parent session.' Children report progress with the framework `task_update` tool; `task_cancel` is available to task owners. Only the child's answer (or structured output when outputSchema is set; for remote agents 'The structured value arrives in the task's completion notification') returns; no child transcript. 'A child parks after answering instead of terminating, keeping its session and conversation history alive'; continuation by agentId; AGENT_MISMATCH / AGENT_BUSY errors; unknown or omitted agentId starts a new child. Parent stream carries subagent.called / subagent.completed and proxied input.requested / authorization.* events; child progress is followable by subscribing to GET /eve/v1/session/:childSessionId/stream (observer side, not injected into the parent model).
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: Children: no sibling visibility documented; nothing is injected into a child beyond `message` (children of the root copy share the root sandbox, so file writes are mutually visible: 'Give parallel children non-overlapping write scopes'). Parent side: '[Agents]' roster: 'Whenever the set of parked (resumable) children changes, eve appends a framework-injected note to the conversation — labeled [Agents] and carrying an <agents> block — listing each child's agentId, name, and latest status. The static system prompt tells the model the note is injected by eve, not written by the user'; appended only when the listing changes, most recent note authoritative, running children absent until they park. This is a parent-visible child ledger; children do not receive it. Parent handles die with the parent session (local children terminated, remote children reset best-effort).
harness.knobs: Tool call { message: string; agentId?: string; outputSchema?: object } (message is the only parent-to-child context channel); defineAgent({ description (required), model, instructions }) under agent/subagents/<id>/ with own tools/, extensions/, skills/, sandbox/, subagents/ (schedules/ root-only); defineDynamic to expose a subagent conditionally per session or turn (null omits it from the parent's tools); extension-contributed subagents namespaced as <mount>__<id> (e.g. crm__reviewer); defineRemoteAgent / remote agents (outputSchema on the definition or per call); disableTool() at agent/tools/agent.ts removes the built-in copy tool; task_update / task_cancel; subagent model calls retry transient failures at most three times.
harness.static_instruction_confound: Root copies inherit the root's authored instructions, skills, connections, hooks and extension contributions, so anything in the root's instructions.md reaches the copy; declared subagents get only their own instructions.{md,ts} and skills. No repository-wide instruction file (AGENTS.md-style) is documented as auto-loaded (eve's /agents.md is a site discovery page, not an agent input).
harness.evidence_quote: all context the child needs; it never sees the parent's history

harness.harness: OpenAI Codex subagents (CLI /agent threads, IDE extension, ChatGPT desktop app, ChatGPT Work; custom agent TOML files; Auto-review reviewer agent)
harness.default_visibility: Parent conversation: NOT STATED. The raw subagents page (markdown re-read in full) contains no sentence saying whether a spawned 'agent thread' sees the parent thread's history; the words 'history' and 'conversation' do not appear in that sense. Documented parent-to-child channels: (a) the spawn prompt Codex writes ('A good subagent prompt should explain how to divide the work, whether Codex should wait for all agents before continuing, and what summary or output to return'); (b) configuration inheritance: 'If you don't configure a subagent model or model_reasoning_effort, the subagent inherits the parent agent's model and reasoning effort'; 'Other session settings, such as sandbox_mode, mcp_servers, and skills.config, inherit from the parent when the custom agent file omits them'; 'Subagents inherit your current sandbox policy'; 'Codex also reapplies the parent turn's live runtime overrides when it spawns a child'; (c) AGENTS.md and skills: 'Codex loads these files as configuration layers for spawned sessions' (custom agent files) and delegation can be triggered 'when applicable AGENTS.md or skill instructions request it'. Built-in agents: default, worker, explorer. Design guidance: 'Keep the main agent focused on requirements, decisions, and final outputs'; 'Return summaries from subagents instead of raw intermediate output.' ChatGPT Work: 'Subagents use the tools available to the parent chat'; Ultra intelligence level 'lets ChatGPT proactively delegate suitable work to subagents'. Auto-review reviewer (separate mechanism, auto-review page): 'The reviewer is itself a Codex agent with a narrower job than the main agent: decide whether a specific boundary-crossing action should run. The reviewer sees a compact transcript plus the exact approval request. That typically includes user messages, surfaced assistant updates, relevant tool calls and tool outputs, and the action now being proposed for approval. It can also perform read-only checks to gather missing context, but it does so rarely. Hidden assistant reasoning is not included. Auto-review sees retained chat items and tool evidence, not private chain-of-thought.' So the reviewer is the one Codex child with a documented (compact, V4-like) transcript view; work subagents remain undocumented.
harness.returned_to_parent: Consolidated result, not transcript: 'When many agents are running, Codex waits until all requested results are available, then returns a consolidated response'; 'The main thread collects the subagent results into its final response'; the app 'surfaces each subagent thread so you can inspect its work and the summary returned to the main chat'. Approval requests from inactive threads surface to the user (CLI overlay shows the source thread; non-interactive runs fail the action 'and Codex surfaces the error back to the parent workflow'). Auto-review: 'Codex returns the review rationale to the main agent' on denial; reviewer transcripts retained under ~/.codex/sessions.
harness.sibling_or_ledger_visibility: Not documented. No statement that agent threads see, message, or share state with each other; orchestration ('spawning new subagents, routing follow-up instructions, waiting for results, and closing agent threads') is done by the main thread. The user can steer, stop, or close a running subagent by asking Codex; /agent switches threads in the CLI; the web sidebar 'doesn't provide controls to stop or steer an individual subagent'. No shared ledger or peer-status primitive.
harness.knobs: Spawn prompt (model-authored). [agents] config (config reference, verbatim): agents.enabled boolean 'Enable or disable multi-agent tools (default: true)'; agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session number 'Maximum number of spawned-agent threads that can be open concurrently, excluding the primary thread. When unset, Codex chooses the default'; agents.max_threads 'Legacy alias'; agents.default_subagent_model / agents.default_subagent_reasoning_effort (explicit spawn values take precedence); agents.interrupt_message boolean 'Record a model-visible message when an agent turn is interrupted (default: true)' (subagents page: 'Set it to false to omit the model-visible interruption message from the agent's context'); agents.<name>.config_file 'Path to a TOML config layer for that role'; agents.<name>.description 'Role guidance shown to Codex when choosing and spawning that agent type'. NO agents.max_depth key exists anywhere in the configuration reference (the only max_depth key is permissions.<name>.filesystem.glob_scan_max_depth). Custom agent files (~/.codex/agents/ or .codex/agents/): required name, description, developer_instructions; optional model, model_reasoning_effort, sandbox_mode, mcp_servers, skills.config; resolution order explicit spawn value, then [agents] default, then parent value, file wins for model/effort; a custom agent named like a built-in overrides it.
